ERGODICITY AND IRREVERSIBILITY

遍历性和不可逆性

A t the beginning of this book, we saw how skiing is non-ergodic. An injury can cause a skier’s championship to be over, nullifying any future wins he could have collected in the remaining races. It might even cause his career to be over, nullifying any future earnings he could have made.

本书开头我们就了解到，滑雪运动并非遍历性运动。一次伤病就可能终结一名滑雪运动员的冠军头衔，使他在剩余比赛中可能获得的任何胜利都化为乌有。伤病甚至可能终结他的职业生涯，使他未来可能获得的任何收入都付之东流。

We also saw how investing is non-ergodic too. Bankruptcy is a form of game-over. It prevents you from collecting any future profit that your ventures might have made had they survived.

我们也看到，投资也是非遍历性的。破产就等于游戏结束。它会让你无法获得任何原本可能从你的企业获得的利润，即使这些利润原本是企业如果存活下来所获得的。

Then , we saw how a healthcare system can work on average and still fail locally. This is because those who died do not resuscitate once a hospital works again. Death is a form of game-over: it nullifies any future gain.

然后，我们看到，即使医疗系统平均运转良好，局部地区仍然可能出现问题。这是因为，即使医院恢复运转，那些已经去世的人也无法被救活。死亡就像游戏结束：它抹杀了未来所有可能的希望。

Finally , we saw how public transportation is non-ergodic. You lose a flight when the train is late but do not gain a plane ticket when it arrives early. When being late is a form of game-over, it brings non-ergodicity.

最后，我们看到了公共交通的非遍历性。火车晚点会让你错过航班，但火车提前到达并不意味着你会获得一张机票。当晚点意味着游戏结束时，它就体现了非遍历性。

Here is the common thread: game-overs bring non-ergodicity.

共同点在于：游戏结束会导致非遍历性。

# ↩

Irreversibility

不可逆性

The concept of the previous page can be generalized as follows: irreversibility brings non-ergodicity.

上一页的概念可以概括如下：不可逆性导致非遍历性。

After a game-over, you cannot keep playing. Game -overs are a form of irreversibility, but they are not the only ones. Below is another.

游戏结束后，你就无法继续游戏了。游戏结束是一种不可逆状态，但并非唯一的不可逆状态。下面是另一种。

As Nassim Nicholas Taleb noted, in some societies, if you’re poor, you’re likely to stay poor, and if you’re rich, you’re likely to stay rich. In these societies, one cannot assume that the lifetime outcome of a person born poor will coincide with the average of the population. They are likely to stay below average. Such a society in which wealth is at least partially irreversible is non-ergodic. 1

正如纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布所指出的，在某些社会中，如果你贫穷，你很可能一直贫穷；如果你富有，你很可能一直富有。在这些社会中，我们不能假设一个出身贫寒的人的一生境遇会与人口平均水平一致。他们很可能始终低于平均水平。这种财富至少部分不可逆转的社会是非遍历的。

# ↩

The ergodicity test

遍历性检验

Here is a simple test to estimate whether a situation is ergodic. “ Are there irreversible consequences?” If yes, it is non-ergodic.

这里有一个简单的测试方法来判断一个情境是否是遍历的。“是否存在不可逆的后果？” 如果是，则该情境是非遍历的。

This test is incomplete. It doesn’t identify all non-ergodic situations. However , a positive answer does imply that the situation at hand is non-ergodic.

这个测试并不完整，它无法识别所有非遍历情况。但是，肯定的回答确实意味着当前情况是非遍历的。

In that case, avoid advice that neglects sources of irreversibility. 2

在这种情况下，应避免提供忽略不可逆因素的建议。

1 Also consider the later chapter on ergodicity as a non-binary concept.

1 另请参阅后面关于遍历性作为非二元概念的章节。

2 Their technical name is absorption barriers.

2 它们的专业名称是吸收屏障。

# ↩
19
# ↩

ERGODICITY AND EXPOSURE

遍历性和暴露性

T here is a common misconception that ergodicity or non-ergodicity are properties of an activity. They are not. Take Russian Roulette , for example. It is non-ergodic for the gambler playing it but is rather ergodic for an imaginary company contracting gamblers to play. For this company, gamblers are replaceable. If enough time passes between rounds so that the company has the time to recruit new gamblers to substitute dead ones, its lifetime outcome will match its population outcome. 1

人们普遍误解遍历性或非遍历性是活动的固有属性。事实并非如此。以俄罗斯轮盘赌为例。对于参与赌博的赌徒而言，它是非遍历的；但对于一家假想的公司而言，它却是遍历的。这家公司雇佣赌徒参与赌博，而赌徒是可以替换的。如果每轮游戏之间间隔足够长的时间，公司有时间招募新的赌徒来替换死亡的赌徒，那么公司的最终结果将与人口结果一致。

Therefore , ergodicity is not just the property of an activity. Instead , ergodicity is a property of an activity, its participants, and the exposure of the latter to the former – in short, of a system.

因此，遍历性不仅仅是活动的属性。相反，遍历性是活动的属性，也是参与者的属性，以及参与者与活动的接触的属性——简而言之，是系统的属性。

# ↩

Ergodicity – for individual and for systems

遍历性——对于个体和系统而言

Nassim Nicholas Taleb made a similar point. In his words, “ My death at Russian Roulette is not ergodic for me, but it is ergodic for the system.”

纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布也表达了类似的观点。用他的话说，“我在俄罗斯轮盘赌中的死亡对我个人而言并非必然，但对整个系统而言却是必然的。”

Also , in his Antifragile , he pointed out how, for a species to be antifragile (adapt and therefore resist change), its members must be fragile. Natural selection is a mechanism that benefits a species 2 but requires the death of some of its members. If the members were nearly invincible, then the species would lose the capacity to adapt.

此外，他在《反脆弱》一书中指出，一个物种要想具备反脆弱性（即适应环境并因此抵抗变化），其成员本身就必须足够脆弱。自然选择是一种有利于物种的机制，但需要部分成员的死亡。如果物种成员几乎刀枪不入，那么该物种就会丧失适应能力。

Ergodicity is scale-dependent . A system observed at some scale may show a different ergodicity than the same system observed at a different scale.

遍历性与尺度有关。在某一尺度下观测到的系统，其遍历性可能与在另一尺度下观测到的同一系统不同。

# ↩

Practical implications

实际意义

It’s good news that ergodicity depends not only on the activity performed but also on your exposure to it. It means that if you limit your exposure to non-ergodicity, you can still participate in non-ergodic activities almost as if they were ergodic.

好消息是，遍历性不仅取决于所进行的活动，还取决于你接触该活动的频率。这意味着，即使你限制自己接触非遍历性活动，你仍然可以参与非遍历性活动，几乎就像参与遍历性活动一样。

The following chapter will teach you how to do it. Meanwhile , here are a few examples of methods that make you much less likely to hit a “game-over:”

下一章将教你如何做到这一点。同时，这里有一些方法可以大大降低你遇到“游戏结束”的几率：

  • Instead of going all-in on a single bet, take many independent bets. 3
    不要孤注一掷，而是进行多次独立投注。
  • Use protections (of all kinds – Personal Protective Equipment , insurance, capped-downside options, and so on).
    使用各种防护措施（个人防护装备、保险、风险控制方案等）。
  • Set aside some buffers and reserves (of money, time, trust, etc.) so that even if you lose everything you committed to an activity, you still have some set aside to recover. 4
    预留一些缓冲和储备（金钱、时间、信任等），这样即使你投入到某项活动中的所有努力都付诸东流，你仍然有一些储备可以用来弥补损失。

1 For the company, Russian Roulette is not fully ergodic, due to the small but nonzero possibility that most or all gamblers die at the same time, or that after a streak of bad luck, so many gamblers die that the company goes bankrupt. Theoretically, ergodicity is a binary property. However, it’s evident how “Russian Roulette is less non-ergodic when played by a company rather than a single gambler” is a meaningful statement. More on this in the later chapter on the non-binary interpretation of ergodicity.

1. 对公司而言，俄罗斯轮盘赌并非完全遍历，因为存在着大多数或所有赌客同时死亡的可能性（虽然很小但并非为零），或者在一连串的坏运气之后，大量赌客死亡导致公司破产。理论上，遍历性是一个二元属性。然而，显而易见，“由公司而非单个赌客进行俄罗斯轮盘赌时，其非遍历性程度更低”这一论断是有意义的。关于遍历性的非二元解释，我们将在后续章节中进行更详细的探讨。

2 Within a certain range. Natural selection benefits a species when it kills a moderate part of its population and harms it when it kills a large part of it (or even drives it extinct).

2 在一定范围内。自然选择在杀死适量种群数量时有利于物种，而在杀死大量种群数量时则对物种有害（甚至导致物种灭绝）。

I clarify and expand this concept in my video “A visual framework for antifragility,” youtube.com/watch?v=cZnu9Slpq_U

我在视频“反脆弱性的可视化框架”中阐明并扩展了这个概念，视频链接：youtube.com/watch?v=cZnu9Slpq_U

3 Make sure that they are really independent, though! A real estate investor is not really diversifying by purchasing two buildings in the same city. Or, to be more precise, he is diversifying against some risks (e.g., an explosion from a gas leak) but not against others (e.g., the city losing jobs).

3 但一定要确保它们真正独立！房地产投资者在同一城市购买两栋楼并不能真正实现风险分散。或者更准确地说，他分散的是某些风险（例如，煤气泄漏引发的爆炸），而不是其他风险（例如，城市失业）。

4 Note that those buffers need to be really separate. Using Friday afternoons as a buffer only works if you don’t schedule activities within them until the very last minute; using $10k in a savings account as a buffer only works if you do not use them to double down on a lousy investment; and so on.

4 请注意，这些缓冲时间必须真正独立。将周五下午用作缓冲时间，只有在你直到最后一刻才安排活动的情况下才有效；将储蓄账户中的 1 万美元用作缓冲时间，只有在你不将其用于加倍投入糟糕的投资的情况下才有效；等等。

# ↩

ERGODICITY AS A NON-BINARY PROPERTY

遍历性作为一种非二元属性

F ormally , ergodicity is a binary property. A system is either ergodic or not – nothing in between. The lifetime outcomes of its participants either coincide with its population outcome or they don’t – nothing in between.

从形式上看，遍历性是一个二元属性。一个系统要么是遍历的，要么不是遍历的——不存在中间状态。其参与者的终生结果要么与总体结果一致，要么不一致——不存在中间状态。

In theory, this is a useful distinction. If you can choose between acting in an ergodic or non-ergodic context, choose the former. However , most practical contexts are non-ergodic. Work , sports, relationships, and real life are all non-ergodic. They all contain some degree of irreversibility. You cannot just refuse to engage in non-ergodic activities.

理论上，这是一个有用的区分。如果可以选择在遍历性情境或非遍历性情境中行动，那就选择前者。然而，大多数实际情境都是非遍历性的。工作、运动、人际关系和现实生活都是非遍历性的。它们都包含一定程度的不可逆性。你不能仅仅因为是非遍历性活动就拒绝参与。

It becomes then useful to expand the concept of ergodicity from black and white to a scale of shades. This way, we can access more practical considerations such as “ How can I make my business more ergodic?”

因此，将遍历性的概念从非黑即白扩展到一系列细微差别就变得很有意义。这样，我们就可以考虑更多实际问题，例如“如何让我的业务更具遍历性？”

In the previous chapter’s example, a company hiring Russian Roulette players is not a truly ergodic activity. There are still points of irreversibility. For example, a streak of bad luck in which all gamblers die might still bankrupt the company. However , for all practical purposes, the assertion “ Russian Roulette is more ergodic if played by a company contracting gamblers rather than by a single gambler” makes a lot of sense.

在前一章的例子中，一家公司雇佣俄罗斯轮盘赌玩家并非真正意义上的遍历性活动。其中仍然存在不可逆性。例如，如果运气极差，所有赌徒全部丧命，公司仍然可能破产。然而，就实际应用而言，“如果由一家公司雇佣赌徒而非单个赌徒来玩俄罗斯轮盘赌，则该活动更具遍历性”这一论断是很有道理的。

This means that, in the medium term, the lifetime outcome is closer to that of its population for a company than for a single player.

这意味着，从中长期来看，公司的终身业绩更接近其人口的整体业绩，而单个玩家的终身业绩则更接近其人口的整体业绩。

# ↩

Finite time horizons

有限的时间范围

Real -life players do not care about infinite time horizons; they care about finite ones. Only mathematicians and philosophers care about infinite time frames; entrepreneurs and workers care about the time frame their job is supposed to last. For example, an investment banker might only care about whether his investments will produce ergodic returns in the time frame he is expected to remain at his job.

现实生活中的参与者并不关心无限的时间跨度，他们关心的是有限的时间跨度。只有数学家和哲学家才会关心无限的时间框架；企业家和员工关心的是他们工作预计持续的时间。例如，一位投资银行家可能只关心他的投资在他预计任职的期限内是否能产生遍历性回报。

This doesn’t mean that people don’t care about negative events with a mean-time-to-happen higher than their time horizon. A rational entrepreneur with a 10-year time horizon still cares about a risk that is expected to materialize every 11 years.

但这并不意味着人们不关心平均发生时间长于自身投资期限的负面事件。一个理性的企业家，即使投资期限为10年，仍然会关注预计每11年发生一次的风险。

Instead , it means that people neglect events that don’t create a meaningful gap between lifetime and population outcomes when measured over the time horizon of their concern.

相反，这意味着人们会忽略那些在他们所关注的时间范围内衡量时，不会在终身结果和人口结果之间造成实质性差距的事件。

# ↩

Ergodicity and decision-making

遍历性和决策

Because of the human tendency to operate on finite time horizons, if you studied ergodicity to increase your chances of achieving your goals or to understand human behavior, a black-and-white definition of ergodicity that considers infinite timeframes does little good. It is more effective to study ergodicity on medium-term timeframes.

由于人类倾向于在有限的时间范围内行事，如果你研究遍历性是为了提高实现目标的几率或理解人类行为，那么一个考虑无限时间框架的、非黑即白的遍历性定义意义不大。在中期时间框架内研究遍历性更为有效。

To summarize the previous page, most people do not care if an activity has a source of irreversibility. Instead , they care whether irreversibility has a non-negligible chance of manifesting within the period they see themselves performing the activity. In other words, what matters is not whether the lifetime and the population outcomes diverge over infinite time-frames – what matters is if they diverge significantly over the medium term.

总结上一页的内容，大多数人并不关心一项活动是否存在不可逆性。相反，他们关心的是，在他们参与这项活动的这段时间内，这种不可逆性发生的概率是否不容忽视。换句话说，重要的不是个体寿命和群体寿命的结果在无限长的时间尺度上是否会趋于一致，而是它们在中期内是否会发生显著变化。

Russian Roulette – the non-ergodic activity by excellence.

俄罗斯轮盘赌——卓越的非遍历性活动。

Moreover , as pointed out before, people cannot realistically avoid any non-ergodic activity. We all need to perform many of them in our lives. Therefore , people do not only care whether an activity is non-ergodic; they care how much it is.

此外，正如前文所述，人们实际上无法完全避免任何非遍历性活动。我们每个人在生活中都需要进行许多这类活动。因此，人们不仅关心某项活动是否属于非遍历性活动，还关心其非遍历性的程度。

Hence , for most people, what matters is how much the lifetime outcome diverges from the population outcome in the medium term . For example, if the time average of my wealth after 70 years is 90% of its expected value, then it is not meaningless to say that the investment is 90% ergodic. Or , if my investment’s time average equals its expected value in 90% of parallel worlds, it is not meaningless to say it is 90% ergodic.

因此，对大多数人来说，重要的是终身收益与中期总体收益的偏差程度。例如，如果我70年后财富的平均值为预期值的90%，那么说这项投资具有90%的遍历性并非毫无意义。或者说，如果我的投资在90%的平行世界中都等于其预期值，那么说它具有90%的遍历性也并非毫无意义。

Of course, neither is fully correct, and both are actually wrong in some important ways, but here is the thing: the value of such statements is not in whether they are right, but in whether they lead to good follow-up questions, such as, “how do I make my investment more ergodic?”

当然，两者都不完全正确，而且在某些重要方面实际上都是错误的，但关键在于：此类陈述的价值不在于它们是否正确，而在于它们是否能引出好的后续问题，例如，“我如何使我的投资更具遍历性？”

This is the justification for my use, within this book, of a non-binary interpretation of ergodicity.

这就是我在本书中使用遍历性非二元解释的理由。

# ↩

The irreversibility of time

时间的不可逆性

In most of the examples described so far, non-ergodicity caused a permanent loss of money, health, reputation, or other assets. There is one more resource we lose permanently: time.

在目前描述的大多数例子中，非遍历性都导致了金钱、健康、名誉或其他资产的永久性损失。还有一种资源我们会永久损失：时间。

No calculation, thought experiment, or study can pretend to model real-life behavior if it assumes time is infinite. Such an arbitrary and unwarranted assumption can lead to misclassifying an irrational behavior as rational or the other way around.

如果假设时间是无限的，那么任何计算、思想实验或研究都无法模拟现实生活中的行为。这种武断且毫无根据的假设会导致将非理性行为误判为理性行为，反之亦然。

# ↩

The Ludic fallacy

游戏谬误

I first learned about the Ludic Fallacy from Nassim Nicholas Taleb . He made the following thought experiment: imagine that a coin falls ten times in a row on its “heads” side. What are the chances of it falling “heads” on the eleventh flip? If you answered, “50% because flips are independent,” you committed the Ludic Fallacy – you assumed that the rules described the game, failing to consider the possibilities of the coin being uneven or the flipper being a skilled swindler.

我第一次接触到游戏谬误是从纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布那里。他做了这样一个思想实验：假设一枚硬币连续十次正面朝上，那么第十一次正面朝上的概率是多少？如果你回答“50%，因为每次抛掷都是独立的”，那么你就犯了游戏谬误——你假定规则描述的是游戏本身，而忽略了硬币本身可能不均匀，或者抛掷者是个老练的骗子。

As Tim Hoffman noted, 1 the Ludic Fallacy may lead us to believe that some situations are ergodic while they aren’t. This is o ne more reason not to fixate on a binary interpretation of ergodicity.

正如蒂姆·霍夫曼所指出的，游戏谬误可能会让我们误以为某些情况是遍历的，而实际上并非如此。这又是一个不应执着于对遍历性进行二元解释的原因。

1 https://twitter.com/manoeuver/status/1450497965735485443?s=21

1 https://twitter.com/manoeuver/status/1450497965735485443?s=21

# ↩

IN SEARCH OF ERGODICITY

探寻遍历性

I n the book so far, we have seen the problem with non-ergodicity: it causes your lifetime outcome to be worse than the expected one.

到目前为止，我们已经看到了非遍历性的问题：它会导致你的一生结果比预期结果更糟。

In many situations, you want to increase the ergodicity of the systems you’re a part of. For example, if you are an investor, the less ergodic your investments are, the lower their lifetime returns. 1 Hence , you want to make your investments as ergodic as possible. 2 Similarly , if you are the manager of an organization, you want to increase its ergodicity – so that a downturn doesn’t make it go out of business. The same applies if you are a freelancer.

在许多情况下，您都希望提高所处系统的遍历性。例如，如果您是投资者，投资的遍历性越低，其长期收益就越低。因此，您需要尽可能提高投资的遍历性。同样，如果您是组织的管理者，您也希望提高组织的遍历性，以避免经济衰退导致组织倒闭。自由职业者的情况也类似。

The rest of this book acknowledges this need. It presents you with three strategies that you can use to make a system more ergodic. 3

本书的其余部分也承认这种需求。它向您介绍了三种可用于使系统更具遍历性的策略。

1 All other things being equal.

1 在其他条件相同的情况下。

2 Here, and for the rest of the book, I refer to (non)ergodicity as a non-binary property. The motivations have been explained in the previous pages.

2 在这里，以及本书的其余部分，我将（非）遍历性视为一种非二元属性。其动机已在前文中解释过。

3 Some readers might have recognized that there are situations in which you want to prevent something from surviving. For example, cancer, or zombie companies in a bull market. This is still about increasing ergodicity – at the higher layer. For example, introducing irreversibility so that zombie companies go bankrupt decreases the ergodicity of companies but increases the ergodicity of the market. This relationship between survival at different layers is explored more in detail in my 2018 book “The Power of Adaptation.”

3 有些读者可能已经意识到，在某些情况下，我们需要阻止某些事物存活下来。例如，癌症，或者牛市中的僵尸企业。这仍然关乎提高遍历性——在更高层面上。例如，引入不可逆性，使僵尸企业破产，会降低企业的遍历性，但会提高市场的遍历性。我在2018年出版的《适应的力量》一书中更详细地探讨了不同层面上的生存关系。

# ↩
PART IV
第四部分
# ↩

REDUCING EXPOSURE

减少接触

One source of non-ergodicity is irrecoverable situations, or “game-overs.” For example, bankruptcy, death, social ostracization, and permanent injuries. It is natural, then, that the first of the three strategies to manage non-ergodicity is to reduce exposure to game-over.

非遍历性的一个来源是不可逆转的情况，或者说“游戏结束”。例如，破产、死亡、社会排斥和永久性伤害。因此，应对非遍历性的三种策略中的第一种自然是减少遭遇“游戏结束”的情况。

The simplest and surest way to do so is to refuse to participate in any activity that has such a risk. Duh .

最简单、最稳妥的办法就是拒绝参与任何有此类风险的活动。这还用说吗？

This works great in theory. However , in real life, we can seldom adopt such a strategy. We cannot decide not to leave our house for fear of incidents. Nor can we keep all our money in a safe – if we did, inflation would erode our wealth.

理论上这当然行得通。然而，在现实生活中，我们很少能采取这样的策略。我们不可能因为害怕发生意外就足不出户。我们也不能把所有的钱都放在保险箱里——如果那样做，通货膨胀会侵蚀我们的财富。

In real life, two better options are what Nassim Nicholas Taleb calls a Barbell strategy and the Kelly Criterion – the topics of the next two chapters.

在现实生活中，还有两种更好的选择，分别是纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布所说的杠铃策略和凯利准则——接下来两章的主题。

# ↩
22
# ↩

THE BARBELL STRATEGY

杠铃策略

T he barbell is a piece of gym equipment in which most of the weight is at the sides, with a long stick in between. It is more effective than a regular rod of the same weight.

杠铃是一种健身器材，其大部分重量集中在两侧，中间由一根长杆连接。它比同等重量的普通杠铃更有效。

Crossing the street to pick up a banknote is an activity that behaves like Russian Roulette – but only if observed over long time frames.For normal people with a finite life expectancy, who might engage in the activity only a few times during their lives, it is an ergodic activity for most practical purposes.

过马路捡钞票的行为就像玩俄罗斯轮盘赌——但这只有在长时间的观察下才会显现出来。对于寿命有限的普通人来说，他们一生中可能只会进行几次这样的行为，因此在大多数实际情况下，这是一种遍历性行为。

In investing, the barbell strategy consists of allocating part of one’s wealth to non-risky assets and part to risky ones with high upside (the asymmetry being reminiscent of a barbell). Investors who do so find themselves wealthier than those investing all their wealth in medium-risk assets (a shape that would remind of a regular rod). 1 One reason is that a medium-risk investment is less likely to suffer large losses but is not immune to them – and, over long-enough timeframes, “less likely” means “eventually.”

在投资中，杠铃策略是指将部分财富配置于低风险资产，部分配置于高收益高风险资产（这种不对称性类似于杠铃）。采用这种策略的投资者往往比那些将所有财富都投资于中等风险资产（类似于普通杠铃）的投资者更加富有。原因之一是，中等风险投资遭受重大损失的可能性较小，但并非完全没有风险——而且，从足够长的时间跨度来看，“可能性较小”意味着“最终还是会遭受损失”。

The barbell strategy consists of exposing most of yourself to safe activities and a tiny bit of yourself to risky ones with high upside.

杠铃策略是指将大部分精力投入到安全的活动中，只投入一小部分精力投入到高风险高回报的活动中。

This is distinct from exposing all of yourself to safe activities 2 most of the time and seldom to risky ones with high upside. Doing so puts you at risk of game-over while you perform the latter. Conversely , the point of the barbell strategy is to pursue risky activities in a way that caps downside risk (not by reducing its frequency but its impact).

这与大部分时间都只参与安全活动，而很少参与高风险高回报的活动截然不同。这样做会让你在进行后者时面临游戏结束的风险。相反，杠铃策略的要点在于以一种能够限制下行风险（不是降低风险频率，而是降低其影响）的方式来参与高风险活动。

The barbell strategy extends beyond investing. In business, it means allocating most of your time to activities with safe returns and just a bit to risky ventures whose success can be life-changing. In life, it means securing your bases and taking small, limited-downside, high-upside bets.

杠铃策略的应用范围远不止投资。在商业领域，它意味着将大部分时间分配给收益稳定的活动，只投入少量时间进行风险较高但成功可能改变人生的项目。在生活中，它意味着夯实基础，并进行一些风险小、收益高的尝试。

This apparently banal strategy is cleverer than it seems. By reducing the amount exposed to risk, it prevents a single loss, or a short series of losses, from constituting a game-over. It also gives you the opportunity, after some bad luck, to “exit” – a luxury that more invested participants lack.

这种看似普通的策略其实比表面看起来更巧妙。它通过减少风险敞口，避免了一次或几次短期亏损就导致游戏结束。此外，它还让你在遭遇一些不幸之后有机会“退出”——这是那些投入更多资金的参与者所不具备的优势。

Moreover , this strategy acknowledges that, in most contexts, a small exposure to high upside brings higher returns than a moderate exposure to moderate upside. This is particularly relevant in contexts where returns cluster. That said, the distribution of returns is not the point here. What matters is that you can afford small risky bets for longer. Otherwise , if you lose a few moderate bets with moderate upside, you’re done.

此外，该策略承认，在大多数情况下，小额高收益投资比中等收益投资带来更高的回报。这一点在收益集中分布的情况下尤为重要。话虽如此，收益分布并非关键所在。重要的是，你能够承受更长时间的小额高风险投资。否则，如果你在几次中等收益的投资中亏损，你的投资生涯就结束了。

# ↩

The barbell strategy and ergodicity

杠铃策略和遍历性

One lesson from Taleb’s work is that risk management is not about prudence but about removing the risks of “game-over” so that you can be aggressive with other risks.

塔勒布的著作告诉我们，风险管理不在于谨慎，而在于消除“游戏结束”的风险，这样你就可以积极应对其他风险。

Similarly , the barbell strategy is not about reducing risk in general. Instead , it is about limiting the part of your assets that are exposed to irreversibility.

同样，杠铃策略并非旨在降低整体风险，而是为了限制暴露于不可逆转风险的资产比例。

A balanced or medium-risk exposure does not do the trick. It would be like playing Russian Roulette with one-in-twelve bullets rather than one-in-six: it just means that the game-over is delayed but does not prevent it. Conversely , the barbell strategy is like playing Russian Roulette without pointing the gun to your skull but at a $100 banknote. If you’re unlucky ( when you’re unlucky), you only lose the banknote, not your life.

均衡或中等风险的配置并不能解决问题。这就像玩俄罗斯轮盘赌，子弹的概率从六分之一变成了十二分之一：这只是延迟了游戏结束的时间，但并不能阻止它。相反，杠铃策略就像玩俄罗斯轮盘赌，枪口不是对准你的脑袋，而是对准一张100美元的钞票。如果你运气不好（当你运气不好的时候），你只会损失这张钞票，而不会失去生命。

Accordingly , here is an alternative formulation of the barbell strategy. “ Preserve your ergodicity by investing in non-ergodic activities only what can be lost without endangering the whole.”

因此，这里提供一种杠铃策略的替代表述：“通过投资于非遍历性活动来保持遍历性，但只投资那些即使损失也不会危及整体的活动。”

# ↩

Applying the barbell strategy

应用杠铃策略

As a professional, I apply the barbell strategy by always looking for new business opportunities but never entering any in such a full and decisive manner that a failure could endanger my livelihood.

作为一名专业人士，我运用杠铃策略，总是寻找新的商机，但从不以过于彻底和果断的方式进入任何一个项目，以免失败危及我的生计。

I also apply the barbell strategy with my investments, allocating most of my money to safe “high-ergodicity assets” and taking small speculative bets with the rest.

我的投资组合也采用了杠铃策略，将大部分资金分配给安全的“高遍历性资产”，其余资金则用于小额投机性投资。

More in general, I look for risk but make sure that I never approach it in such a way that an unexpected event might irreversibly affect my life in any significant matter.

总的来说，我会寻找风险，但会确保我永远不会以任何方式去冒险，以免意外事件对我的生活造成任何重大且不可逆转的影响。

“ Ergodicity is not free.”

STEFANO PERON

“遍历性并非免费。”——斯特凡诺·庇隆

Ergodicity helps us survive and thus grab eventual future gains, but it also comes with opportunity costs. If you limit your exposure to risk, you often limit your exposure to upsides, too. For example, if you limit your investment portfolio exposure to stocks, you also limit your gains from an eventual bull market and thus expose yourself to other negative events. 3

遍历性有助于我们生存并最终获得未来的收益，但它也伴随着机会成本。如果你限制风险敞口，通常也会限制收益机会。例如，如果你将投资组合的股票配置比例限制在一定范围内，你也会限制未来牛市带来的收益，从而让自己面临其他负面事件的风险。

That’s okay. Hopefully , this book gave you the tools to justify to yourself and others that the long-term benefits of avoiding game-overs are well worth the opportunity costs.

没关系。希望这本书能让你掌握必要的工具，从而向自己和他人证明，避免游戏结束带来的长期收益远大于其机会成本。

# ↩

A summary of the first strategy

第一种策略概述

The Barbell strategy is about limiting exposure so that the worst-case scenario doesn’t endanger your survival. It makes the non-ergodic ergodic for most practical purposes.

杠铃策略旨在限制风险暴露，从而避免最坏情况危及生命。它使非遍历性问题在大多数实际应用中成为遍历性问题。

In practice, it consists of investing a large part of yourself in limited-downside activities and a small part in high-upside ones. In particular, an activity with a tiny chance of a ruinous outcome is not considered “limited-downside.”

在实践中，这种策略意味着将大部分资金投入到风险较小的活动中，而将少量资金投入到收益较大的活动中。尤其需要注意的是，那些极有可能导致破产的活动并不属于“风险较小”的范畴。

1 Over the long term. Counterexamples are prone to survivorship bias. When measuring this effect, we shall be wary of considering the same cohort over the long term, not the whole market full of new entrants.

1. 从长远来看。反例容易受到幸存者偏差的影响。在衡量这种影响时，我们应该注意不要长期只考虑同一批人，而应该考虑充满新进入者的整个市场。

2 Safe = capped downside, as assessed based on properties, not historical data.

2 安全 = 下行风险有限制，根据属性而非历史数据进行评估。

3 Stefano Peron also makes the point that increasing ergodicity with respect to a given risk might increase other risks. For example, a trader with limited stock exposure might get fired by his boss during a bull market, for his returns are temporarily subpar. Again, remember the “The Gambler and the Gamble” chapter.

3 斯特凡诺·贝隆也指出，在给定风险下提高遍历性可能会增加其他风险。例如，股票敞口有限的交易员在牛市期间可能会被老板解雇，因为他的收益暂时低于预期。再次提醒，请回顾“赌徒与赌博”一章的内容。

THE KELLY CRITERION

凯利准则

L et’s imagine you play the following game. You have $100. Your ten best friends take turns shooting a ball into a basket. Before each shoot, you decide how much to bet on the shot. If it goes in, you double your bet. If it goes out, you lose your bet. What strategy maximizes your gains?

假设你玩以下游戏。你有100美元。你的十个好朋友轮流投篮。每次投篮前，你都要决定下注金额。如果球进了，你的赌注翻倍；如果球没进，你就输掉赌注。什么策略能使你的收益最大化？

You might have had the following two intuitions. First , you do not want to bet all your money on a single shot. If your friend misses, you lose all your money. You cannot make further bets and thus cannot benefit from eventual wins you could have had in the future. That was the lesson of Russian Roulette : losses absorb future gains.

你可能已经有了以下两种直觉。首先，你不想把所有钱都押在一次赌博上。如果你的朋友没中，你就输光了所有钱。你不能再继续下注，也就无法从未来可能获得的收益中获利。这就是俄罗斯轮盘赌的教训：损失会吞噬未来的收益。

Second , you want to bet more on your friends who are good at basketball and less on the clumsier ones.

其次，你应该多押注那些篮球打得好的朋友，少押注那些比较笨拙的朋友。

These two intuitions, “never go all-in, no matter how tempting the odds” and “payoffs determine the relative size of the bet,” summarize a betting strategy known as the Kelly Criterion , named after the mathematician who invented it. I won’t cover the exact formula because this book aims to build an intuitive understanding of ergodicity, not a mathematical one. What matters is that risk exposure must depend on payoffs and, anyway, be limited.

“无论赔率多么诱人，都不要孤注一掷”和“收益决定投注的相对大小”这两条直觉概括了一种被称为凯利准则的投注策略，该准则以其发明者——数学家凯利的名字命名。我不会赘述具体的公式，因为本书旨在帮助读者建立对遍历性的直观理解，而非数学上的推导。重要的是，风险敞口必须取决于收益，并且无论如何都必须受到限制。

# ↩

How I applied the Kelly Criterion to my life

我如何将凯利准则应用于我的生活中

I routinely use the Kelly Criterion . 1 As an author, consultant, and researcher, I spend most of my time writing books and essays, working with clients, and doing research. All of these projects take time, and time is money. If I invested all my time for the next three years on a single project or client, I would be in a terrible condition in case of failure. Instead , I allocate my time on a per-project basis. Usually , the larger the upside, the more time I spend on the project. However , I always make sure never to commit all of my time to a single project running for an extended time. Too much to lose, both in case the project doesn’t go well or in terms of opportunity costs.

我经常使用凯利准则。作为一名作家、顾问和研究员，我大部分时间都花在写作、撰写文章、服务客户和进行研究上。所有这些项目都需要时间，而时间就是金钱。如果我把未来三年的所有时间都投入到一个项目或客户身上，一旦失败，我将损失惨重。因此，我会根据每个项目的具体情况来分配时间。通常情况下，收益越大，我投入的时间就越多。但是，我始终确保不会把所有时间都投入到一个长期进行的项目中。因为无论项目进展如何，损失都太大了，而且机会成本也很高。

1 Formally, f* = [ p (b + 1) - 1] / b

1 形式上，f* = [ p (b + 1) - 1] / b

Where:

在哪里：

f* is the fraction of the current bankroll to wager; (i.e., how much to bet, expressed in fraction),

f* 是当前资金中用于下注的比例；（即，用分数表示的下注金额），

b is the net fractional odds received on the wager. E.g., if on a $10 the win is $4 plus the wager, then b = 0.4.

b 是投注所得的净赔率。例如，如果投注 10 美元，赢的金额为 4 美元加上投注金额，则 b = 0.4。

p is the probability of a win.

p 是获胜的概率。

THE KELLY CRITERION IN NATURE

自然界的凯利准则

I t’s fascinating that some animals, including us humans, have two psychological processes that, together, approximate the Kelly Criterion . 1 They are moods and fears. The following two pages describe them.

令人着迷的是，包括我们人类在内的一些动物，拥有两种心理过程，这两种过程结合起来近似符合凯利准则。它们分别是情绪和恐惧。以下两页将对此进行描述。

# ↩

Moods and the Kelly Criterion

情绪与凯利准则

In our society, many see being moody as a problem. This is true to some extent, but moods are generally beneficial. For example, consider two hunter-gatherers, Alice and Bob . They live in a territory where the main source of food is berries growing under bushes. Some bushes have no berries, whereas others are full of them. Gathering them is a tiring activity, for one has to walk close to a bush and lift some of its leaves to know whether it contains any berries. Bob is moody, whereas Alice cannot feel any mood. Who do you think is a better gatherer, all other things being equal?

在我们的社会里，许多人把情绪波动视为一种问题。这在某种程度上是正确的，但情绪波动通常是有益的。例如，假设有两个狩猎采集者，爱丽丝和鲍勃。他们生活在一个主要食物来源是灌木丛下浆果的地区。有些灌木丛上没有浆果，而有些则结满了浆果。采集浆果是一项很累人的活动，因为必须走到灌木丛旁，拨开一些叶子才能知道里面是否有浆果。鲍勃情绪波动很大，而爱丽丝则不会有任何情绪波动。在其他条件相同的情况下，你认为谁更擅长采集浆果？

The answer is Bob . He is more likely to check the bushes with berries and not check those without berries. Why is that?

答案是鲍勃。他更有可能检查结了浆果的灌木丛，而不是那些没有浆果的。这是为什么呢？

Well , Alice does not feel any mood, so she tends to sample every bush she walks by – an inefficient method. Conversely , Bob would check the first bush, then the second one; then, he might become discouraged (a mood) and walk for a bit before bending again to check the bush next to him. Once he finds some berries, he gets excited (another mood) and checks all the bushes nearby. This is advantageous because, in nature, resources tend to cluster together. If a bush is particularly fruitful, the chances are that the ones around it are also fruitful, because they grow on the same fertile soil.

爱丽丝没什么心情，所以她会随意地查看路过的每一丛灌木——这种方法效率很低。相反，鲍勃会先查看第一丛，再查看第二丛；然后，他可能会感到沮丧（心情好），走一会儿再弯腰查看旁边的灌木。一旦找到浆果，他就会兴奋起来（心情好），然后查看附近所有的灌木。这样做的好处是，在自然界中，资源往往聚集在一起。如果一丛灌木特别丰产，那么它周围的灌木很可能也丰产，因为它们生长在同一片肥沃的土壤上。

Moods are adaptations to environments with clustered resources.

情绪是对资源集中环境的一种适应。

As the hunter-gatherers’ example showed, moderately moody people tend to be more efficient than moodless ones. ( The keyword being “moderately” – as with anything, excesses are bad.)

正如狩猎采集者的例子所示，情绪适度波动的人往往比情绪完全没有波动的人效率更高。（关键词是“适度”——凡事过犹不及。）

This theory of moods, first formulated by a group of researchers named Eldar E ., Rutledge R . B ., Dolan R . J ., and Niv Y ., 2 is interesting. It shows how moods improve effectiveness by making people spend more time on what looks promising and less time on what is likely to be a waste of time. Moreover , they reduce exposition to what is dangerous (wasting time and energy), thereby improving survival. They allow us to adapt to a world where threats and resources are not uniformly distributed. A must, in a non-ergodic world.

这项由Eldar E.、Rutledge R. B.、Dolan R. J.和Niv Y.等研究人员首次提出的情绪理论非常有趣。它揭示了情绪如何通过引导人们将更多时间投入到看似有希望的事情上，减少在可能浪费时间的事情上，从而提高效率。此外，情绪还能减少人们接触危险事物（浪费时间和精力）的机会，进而提高生存能力。它使我们能够适应一个威胁和资源分布不均的世界。这在非遍历性世界中至关重要。

In particular, you might have noticed a similarity with the Kelly Criterion . Moods cause us to intuitively bet more time and energy on activities with high payoffs and less on activities with low payoffs.

尤其值得注意的是，它与凯利准则有相似之处。情绪会影响我们的直觉，让我们倾向于将更多的时间和精力投入到高回报的活动中，而减少对低回报活动的投入。

# ↩

A practical example from my life

我生活中的一个实际例子

A few pages ago, I mentioned how I allocate my time to my projects by informally following the Kelly Criterion . However , I didn’t tell you that my decision on how much time to allocate to a project is rarely deliberate. Rather , it is based on moods such as excitement. As I begin exploring a project, if I find early successes or interesting bits, my excitement grows, and so does the share of my time I decide to allocate to the project. In the end, the result is similar to what I would have obtained had I applied the Kelly Criterion formally.

前几页我提到过，我如何非正式地运用凯利准则来分配项目时间。然而，我没有告诉你们，我决定给一个项目分配多少时间很少是经过深思熟虑的。相反，这往往取决于情绪，比如兴奋程度。当我开始探索一个项目时，如果我发现一些初步的成功或有趣的部分，我的兴奋感就会增强，我决定分配给该项目的时间比例也会随之增加。最终，结果与我正式运用凯利准则所得到的结果类似。

# ↩

Fear and the Kelly Criterion

恐惧与凯利准则

Moods alone would not be enough to approximate the Kelly Criterion , though. Modulating bets based on payoffs is only one of its two components. The other is to avoid going all-in. Fear is an adaptation that helps us with that.

然而，仅凭情绪不足以近似地判断凯利准则。根据收益调整赌注只是其两个组成部分之一。另一个组成部分是避免孤注一掷。恐惧是一种帮助我们做到这一点的适应机制。

If we didn’t feel fear, a few successes in a row would cause us to be in an ecstatic mood and go all-in. Fear helps us maintain some prudence.

如果我们没有恐惧感，连续几次成功就会让我们欣喜若狂，从而孤注一掷。恐惧感帮助我们保持谨慎。

Similarly , a few failures in a row might cause us to abandon our will to do anything. However , fear of missing out, fear of starvation, fear of being labeled as lazy, and similar fears keep us at least somehow motivated and active.

同样，连续几次失败可能会让我们丧失做任何事的意愿。然而，害怕错失机会、害怕挨饿、害怕被贴上懒惰的标签等等，至少在某种程度上能让我们保持动力和积极性。

Fear helps counterbalance moods. Together , they work a bit like the Kelly Criterion , allowing us to adapt to a non-ergodic world.

恐惧有助于平衡情绪。它们共同作用，有点像凯利准则，使我们能够适应非遍历性的世界。

# ↩

Moods and fears are not just about survival

情绪和恐惧不仅仅关乎生存。

There are mathematical demonstrations that the Kelly Criterion is an effective strategy not only for survival but also for wealth maximization. Similarly , moderately moody and fearful people not only avoid dangers but also accumulate more wealth and other resources.

数学证明表明，凯利准则不仅是生存的有效策略，也是财富最大化的有效策略。同样，情绪波动适中且略带恐惧感的人不仅能规避危险，还能积累更多财富和其他资源。

Of course, this only applies to moderately moody and fearful people, not to excessively moody and fearful ones. Excesses are never good. Those who think otherwise have a narrow definition of success or are prone to survivorship bias. Sadly , many artifacts of our modern times, such as sugar-rich foods and gambling, are designed to induce excesses.

当然，这只适用于情绪波动和恐惧程度适中的人，而不适用于情绪波动和恐惧程度过高的人。过犹不及。那些持相反观点的人，要么对成功的定义过于狭隘，要么容易受到幸存者偏差的影响。可悲的是，我们现代社会的许多产物，例如高糖食品和赌博，其设计目的就是为了诱发过度行为。

# ↩

The curse of modernity

现代性的诅咒

I learned on my skin that moods and fears are sometimes fallible. For example, I remember the first time I ate ice cream from a box, as a kid. I couldn’t stop myself. If it weren’t for the box being finite, I would have gone into a sugar overdose. Similarly , I remember the traumatic experience I had the first time our elementary school brought us to swim, and teachers stomped on my hands as I tried to hang on to the pool’s borders. Afterward , I didn’t want to immerse myself in water for months. Sometimes , moods and fears lead to excesses: addictions and trauma.

我从自身经历中体会到，情绪和恐惧有时并不可靠。例如，我记得小时候第一次吃盒装冰淇淋的情景。我根本停不下来。要不是盒子有限，我肯定会摄入过量糖分。同样，我还记得小学第一次带我们去游泳的恐怖经历：老师们踩在我的手上，我拼命想抓住泳池的边缘。之后好几个月，我都不敢下水。有时，情绪和恐惧会导致过度行为：成瘾和创伤。

Moods and fears estimate whether a situation is auspicious or ominous. As with any categorization tool, they are prone to false positives and false negatives. Natural selection caused our brain to adapt to the optimal tradeoff. However , as with any tradeoff, optimal doesn’t mean perfect.

情绪和恐惧会让我们判断某种情况是吉利还是凶险。但任何分类工具都难免出现误报和漏报。自然选择使我们的大脑适应了这种最佳权衡。然而，任何权衡都意味着最佳，但并非完美。

This particularly applies to modern activities that didn’t exist in the past – such as eating ice cream. Our moods and fears adapted to the environment our ancestors evolved in, not to the modern environment in which you and I live ( “ Instincts are the genetic memory of the problems our ancestors faced,” I use to say). In particular, moods and fears become liabilities when we are exposed to artifacts of the modern world designed to take advantage of them – again, such as ice cream.

这一点尤其适用于过去不存在的现代活动——比如吃冰淇淋。我们的情绪和恐惧是适应祖先进化的环境而形成的，而不是适应你我如今生活的现代环境（我常说，“本能是我们祖先所面临问题的基因记忆”）。尤其当我们接触到现代世界那些旨在利用情绪和恐惧的产物时——比如冰淇淋——它们就会变成我们的负担。

That said, even though they are sometimes wrong, moods and fears are still important assets. They are not perfect by any means, but we are better off with them than without.

话虽如此，尽管情绪和恐惧有时会出错，但它们仍然是重要的认知资源。它们绝非完美无缺，但总比没有它们要好。

1 I do not intend that moods and fears fully reproduce the Kelly criterion, not that they alone approximate it – just that they help approximate it within the range of what is reasonably possible to do with instincts alone.

1 我并不认为情绪和恐惧能够完全重现凯利标准，也不认为它们本身就能近似地达到该标准——只是它们有助于在仅凭本能所能合理达到的范围内近似地达到该标准。

2 “Mood as Representation of Momentum”, Eldar E., Rutledge R. B., Dolan R. J., and Niv Y., 2016.

2 “情绪作为动量的表征”，Eldar E.、Rutledge R. B.、Dolan R. J. 和 Niv Y.，2016 年。

THE KELLY CRITERION AND UNCERTAINTY

凯利准则与不确定性

I n a fantastic article, 1 Harry Crane demonstrates that the Kelly Criterion must be applied more conservatively than the odds of winning would warrant. That’s because, he explains, we seldom know the true odds, and we must take this uncertainty into account.

在一篇精彩的文章中，哈里·克莱恩 (Harry Crane) 论证了凯利准则的应用必须比实际获胜概率更为保守。他解释说，这是因为我们很少能确切知道获胜概率，而我们必须将这种不确定性考虑在内。

Take the example of a gambler who believes having discovered a strategy to bet on horse races that gives him a 10% edge over the gambling house. It would be naïve to think that his real edge is 10%. He believes he has a 10% edge, but he cannot be sure of it until he tries applying the strategy. And if he gambles as if he had a 10% edge before being sure he really has it, he will quickly lose his money in case he’s wrong.

举个例子，假设有个赌徒自认为发现了一种赛马投注策略，能让他比庄家多赢10%。如果认为他真的有10%的优势，那就太天真了。他相信自己有10%的优势，但只有真正运用这种策略才能确定。如果他在还没确定自己真的有10%优势的情况下就贸然下注，一旦判断错误，他很快就会输光所有的钱。

Instead , the optimal strategy is first to bet very conservatively, to test if the edge is real, and only later increase the bets. 2

相反，最佳策略是先非常保守地下注，测试优势是否真实存在，然后再逐步增加赌注。

How conservative should you be, exactly?

究竟应该保守到什么程度？

First of all, decide how much money you’re willing to lose in case you have a bad strategy. For example, you might have $1,000 to invest but be willing to risk only $100. Secondly , size your bets small enough so that by the time you lose $100, you know you have a losing strategy and can stop playing.

首先，你要决定如果策略失误，你愿意承担多少损失。例如，你可能有1000美元的投资资金，但只愿意冒100美元的风险。其次，你的投注额要足够小，这样当你输掉100美元时，你就知道你的策略行不通，可以及时停止游戏。

This last step is critical! Imagine you didn’t follow this reasoning and placed a first bet of $100. If you lose it, you won’t know whether you lost because of a bad strategy or because you got unlucky. You might even be tempted to keep playing and potentially lose more money just to know whether you were right!

最后一步至关重要！想象一下，如果你没有遵循这个逻辑，而是直接下注100美元。如果你输了，你将无法判断输是因为策略错误还是运气不好。你甚至可能会忍不住继续玩下去，结果输掉更多钱，只是为了验证自己的判断是否正确！

Instead , if you place smaller bets, say $5 or $10 each, by the time you lose $100, you will be more certain you had a bad strategy.

相反，如果你每次下注较小的金额，比如 5 美元或 10 美元，那么当你输掉 100 美元时，你就会更加确信你的策略是错误的。

This is why many people use a variation of the Kelly Criterion called “quarter- Kelly ,” where they conservatively bet only 25% of what the Kelly Criterion would deem optimal.

这就是为什么许多人使用凯利准则的变体，称为“四分之一凯利”，他们保守地只下注凯利准则认为的最佳金额的 25%。

As Harry Crane wrote, “ Variance is too much if it prevents us from figuring out what we need to figure out before it’s too late.” And , “ Devise a strategy that allows us to learn about our true edge at a rate we’re comfortable, and to be decisive about quitting once we’ve gained sufficient evidence.”

正如哈里·克莱恩所写，“如果方差过大，以至于我们无法在为时已晚之前弄清楚我们需要弄清楚的事情，那么方差就太大了。”他还说，“制定一种策略，让我们能够以自己感到舒适的速度了解自身的真正优势，并在获得足够的证据后果断地停止。”

# ↩

A summary so far

目前为止的总结

We saw that non-ergodicity is a potentially dangerous condition. You want to make sure you know what you are doing.

我们已经看到，非遍历性是一种潜在的危险情况。你需要确保自己清楚自己在做什么。

The first strategy is to never go all-in on any activity that might result in a game-over in case of misfortune. 3

第一种策略是永远不要孤注一掷地参与任何可能导致游戏结束的活动，因为一旦发生不幸，游戏就会结束。

As seen in the Barbell strategy, this is distinct from never taking any risks. Just take them with limited exposure – for example, by investing just a little. The Kelly Criterion helped you understand how to modulate your bets better.

正如杠铃策略所示，这与完全不承担任何风险截然不同。关键在于控制风险敞口——例如，只投入少量资金。凯利准则能帮助你更好地理解如何调整你的投资策略。

In the next chapter, we will see how the concepts described above apply not only to our actions but also to our society’s. 4

下一章，我们将看到上述概念不仅适用于我们的行为，也适用于我们的社会。

Or, you might discover that you have in your hands a principle that applies at any scale. Either way, you don’t know until you try.

THE PRECAUTIONARY PRINCIPLE

预防原则

T he Precautionary Principle guides us in risk management decisions. It begins by acknowledging that there are two kinds of risks: those that endanger the whole (a population, an ecosystem, the planet) and those that do not.

预防原则指导我们进行风险管理决策。它首先承认风险有两种：一种是危及整体（人口、生态系统、地球）的风险，另一种是不会危及整体的风险。

For example, if someone drives too fast and crashes, he might die, and he might also kill a few people, but the population in general is not affected. This is an example of a risk that can kill an individual without endangering the whole. These risks are safe for the population to take. In some cases, they even make it stronger.

例如，如果有人超速行驶导致车祸，他可能会丧命，也可能造成几人死亡，但总体人群不会受到影响。这就是一种可能导致个体死亡但不会危及整体的风险的例子。这类风险对人群来说是安全的。在某些情况下，它们甚至能增强人群的凝聚力。

Conversely , some risks have the potential to destroy the whole population. We should avoid these risks at all costs.

反之，有些风险则有可能毁灭整个人类。我们应该不惜一切代价避免这些风险。

The Precautionary Principle holds that we should not take risks that endanger the whole, 1 no matter how unlikely. If we keep taking them, we are guaranteed to blow up (remember the Russian Roulette player?).

预防原则认为，我们不应该承担危及整体的风险，无论这种风险发生的可能性多么小。如果我们不断承担这种风险，最终必将导致灾难性的后果（还记得俄罗斯轮盘赌的玩家吗？）。

When they hear about the Precautionary Principle , some reply, “ So what, we never do anything?” This response is wrong, as the next page shows.

当他们听到预防原则时，有些人会回答：“那又怎样，我们什么都不做吗？”这种回答是错误的，下一页将对此进行说明。

# ↩

The Precautionary Principle is not about full prudence

预防原则并非意味着完全谨慎。

The Precautionary Principle does not say to avoid all risks – just those that can destroy the whole. In the words of Nassim Nicholas Taleb , who authored a homonymous paper: 2 “ My death at Russian roulette is not ergodic for me, but it is ergodic for the system. The precautionary principle, in the formulation I did with a few colleagues, is precisely about the highest layer [the system].”

预防原则并非要求规避所有风险，而只是规避那些可能毁灭整体的风险。正如纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布（Nassim Nicholas Taleb）在其同名论文中所述：“我在俄罗斯轮盘赌中丧命对我个人而言并非必然，但对整个系统而言却是必然的。我与几位同事共同提出的预防原则，正是针对最高层（即系统）而言的。”

In other words, feel free to play Russian Roulette by pointing the gun at your skull, but do not play it by pointing the gun at the ecosystem.

换句话说，你可以把枪指着自己的脑袋去玩俄罗斯轮盘赌，但不要把枪指着生态系统去玩。

Nuclear power plants are an example of a risk that, while scary, is contained. No explosion, no matter how deadly to its surroundings, can endanger the planet.

核电站就是一个例子，它虽然令人恐惧，但风险是可控的。任何爆炸，无论对周围环境造成多么致命的破坏，都不会危及地球。

The Precautionary Principle only applies to risks that endanger the whole, not risks that only endanger the local. An example of the latter is nuclear plants – if one blows up, it destroys its surroundings but not the planet. Moreover , a disaster makes other plants less likely to blow up, as we learn about failure points and establish new safety procedures.

预防原则仅适用于危及整体的风险，而不适用于仅危及局部的风险。核电站就是后者的一个例子——如果一座核电站发生爆炸，它只会破坏周围环境，而不会危及整个地球。此外，灾难还能降低其他核电站发生爆炸的可能性，因为我们可以从中了解潜在的故障点并建立新的安全规程。

The Precautionary Principle only applies to risks that can potentially destroy humanity or the ecosystem. 3

预防原则仅适用于可能对人类或生态系统造成毁灭性打击的风险。

# ↩

Risk of ruin and cost-benefit analyses

破产风险和成本效益分析

We saw how we can classify risks into two categories: those with the potential to kill the whole and those without.

我们看到，我们可以将风险分为两类：一类是可能毁灭整体的风险，另一类是不可能毁灭整体的风险。

Here comes the critical bit. We cannot use cost-benefit analysis with risks that can kill the whole. If we take enough risks of this type with a positive cost-benefit analysis, we are guaranteed to kill the whole eventually.

关键就在这里。我们不能用成本效益分析来应对那些可能毁灭整体的风险。如果我们承担足够多的这类风险，却仍然得出正面的成本效益分析结果，那么最终必然会导致整体的毁灭。

In the first chapter of this book, we saw how the expected returns of playing Russian Roulette decrease with the number of times it is played by the same gambler (see the chart below).

本书第一章中，我们看到，对于同一个赌徒来说，玩俄罗斯轮盘赌的预期收益会随着玩的次数增加而减少（见下图）。

The lesson is: do not expose the whole to irreversibility, no matter how attractive the payoffs.

教训是：无论回报多么诱人，都不要让整体面临不可逆转的风险。

For example, an epidemic so deadly that it endangers the human species is a possible systemic risk. Until we have a foolproof demonstration that no virus, no matter how deadly, can endanger humanity, we should take precautions, no matter how costly.

例如，一种致命到足以危及人类的流行病就可能构成系统性风险。在我们能够确凿证明任何病毒，无论多么致命，都不会危及人类之前，我们都应该采取预防措施，无论代价多么高昂。

The most common argument against precautions is that they are expensive. This is not a valid argument. Payoffs are subordinate to ergodicity, so we cannot use them until we can be sure that epidemics are not a systemic risk.

反对采取预防措施最常见的理由是成本高昂。这种说法站不住脚。收益要服从于遍历性，因此，只有当我们确信流行病不会构成系统性风险时，才能使用预防措施。

You cannot compare apples to oranges, nor systemic risks to local ones. The only valid argument in contradiction of a precaution against a systemic risk could be that the precaution itself introduces a similar or larger systemic risk. ( That said, hopefully, the 2020 pandemic showed us the costs of no prevention.) 4

你不能把苹果和橘子相提并论，也不能把系统性风险和局部风险相提并论。唯一能反驳针对系统性风险的预防措施的合理论点，可能是该预防措施本身会引入类似甚至更大的系统性风险。（话虽如此，但愿2020年的疫情让我们看到了不采取预防措施的代价。）

1 What “the whole” is is subjective. For an entrepreneur, his company might be “the whole” worth applying the PP to; for another, it might represent just a venture between others. That said, humanity and the ecosystem are “ the whole” for everyone and thus always worth applying the PP to.

1. “整体”的含义是主观的。对一位企业家而言，他的公司可能就是值得运用绩效原则的“整体”；而对另一位企业家来说，它可能仅仅代表着与其他企业之间的合作。也就是说，对于所有人来说，人类和生态系统都是“整体”，因此始终值得运用绩效原则。

2 The Precautionary Principle (with Application to the Genetic Modification of Organisms), Nassim Nicholas Taleb, Rupert Read, Raphael Douady, Joseph Norman, Yaneer Bar-Yam, 2014.

2 预防原则（及其在生物体基因改造中的应用），纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布、鲁珀特·里德、拉斐尔·杜阿迪、约瑟夫·诺曼、亚尼尔·巴尔-亚姆，2014 年。

3 An example: GMOs.

3 一个例子：转基因生物。

Genetically modified organisms, “GMOs” in short, are plants and animals that scientists genetically modified to bestow them some desirable properties, such as parasite resistance. They are a potential source of good. Some say that they could eradicate malaria or hunger. Sadly, they are also a potential source of harm. For example, it is possible that we create some GMO mosquitoes to fight malaria, and some unexpected interaction causes the initiative to backfire.

转基因生物，简称“GMO”，是指科学家通过基因改造赋予动植物某些优良特性，例如抗寄生虫能力。它们具有潜在的造福人类的潜力。有人认为它们可以根除疟疾或饥饿。然而，令人遗憾的是，它们也可能带来危害。例如，我们可能培育出一些转基因蚊子来对抗疟疾，但某些意想不到的相互作用却导致这一举措适得其反。

Any new technology has a chance of backfiring. However, when they do, most technologies backfire locally. For example, when a nuclear plant explodes, it “only” harms the surrounding territory. Other nuclear plants can be shut down, and the situation can be quickly reassessed, as it happened after the terrible Chernobyl incident in 1986.

任何新技术都有可能产生反作用。然而，即便产生反作用，大多数技术的影响也仅限于局部地区。例如，核电站爆炸“仅仅”会损害周边地区。其他核电站可以关闭，情况也可以迅速重新评估，就像1986年切尔诺贝利核事故后发生的那样。

Conversely, we would have a hard time stopping a GMO that is found harmful after its broad introduction in the ecosystem. Good luck catching GMO mosquitoes.

反之，如果转基因生物在生态系统中广泛引入后被发现有害，我们就很难阻止它。祝你好运，看看能不能抓到转基因蚊子。

Hence, GMOs are risky in a way that nuclear plants aren’t. Only the former have the potential to destroy the ecosystem.

因此，转基因生物的风险与核电站的风险有所不同。只有前者才有可能破坏生态系统。

Note: GMOs didn’t create any systemic problem so far. This doesn’t exclude that they won’t produce any in the future. We just began experimenting with them. Therefore, to estimate their risks, we shall study not the past but the properties of their possible interactions with the ecosystem.

注：转基因生物目前尚未造成任何系统性问题。但这并不排除它们未来不会造成问题。我们才刚刚开始对它们进行试验。因此，为了评估它们的风险，我们应该研究它们与生态系统可能产生的相互作用，而不是过去的情况。

4 The pandemic illustrates the tension between humanity (for which the pandemic could be an existential risk) and the individual (for which both the pandemic and excessive restrictions could be an existential risk). Again, scale matters, and averaging across scales returns a model unrepresentative of reality.

4. 这次疫情凸显了人类（疫情可能构成生存威胁）与个体（疫情和过度限制措施都可能构成生存威胁）之间的紧张关系。再次强调，规模至关重要，跨尺度平均化得到的模型无法代表现实。

NATURAL SELECTION AND FRACTALIZATION

自然选择与分形

N atural selection is a scary process that threatens our livelihoods. However , it is possible to make it work for us rather than against us. In this chapter, I will show you how to harness the power of natural selection.

自然选择是一个令人畏惧的过程，它威胁着我们的生存。然而，我们完全可以让它为我们所用，而不是与我们作对。在本章中，我将向你展示如何驾驭自然选择的力量。

# ↩

Multiscale natural selection

多尺度自然选择

In nature, those who are fit thrive while the unfit perish. Natural selection is a cruel yet essential phenomenon. Without it, humans and civilization as we know it would perhaps not exist.

在自然界，适者生存，不适者淘汰。自然选择残酷却又至关重要。没有它，我们所知的人类和文明或许根本不会存在。

Natural selection also occurs in business. The best companies expand, open new stores, and launch more products, while the worst ones go bankrupt. 1

自然选择也适用于商业领域。优秀的公司会扩张、开设新店、推出更多产品，而最差的公司则会破产。

The same phenomenon applies to the components of companies: employees. The best ones climb in rank. The worst ones get fired.

同样的现象也适用于公司的组成部分：员工。优秀的员工会晋升，而表现差的员工则会被解雇。

An organization that never fires a single employee becomes uncompetitive. Natural selection at the level of the industry will make the company fail. Therefore , to avoid becoming a victim of natural selection, a company must make it act on its employees, at least in a measure.

一个从不解雇任何员工的组织会失去竞争力。行业层面的自然选择最终会导致公司失败。因此，为了避免成为自然选择的牺牲品，公司必须对其员工采取一些措施，至少要有所作为。

Natural selection is inevitable for companies, but they can decide whether it acts on them or within them (in a measure).

自然选择对公司来说是不可避免的，但公司可以选择让自然选择作用于自身还是作用于自身（在一定程度上）。

However , firing employees is not that good either. It has heavy consequences, especially for the fired employee and their family. It is something that we want to avoid within reason.

然而，解雇员工也不是个好办法。它会带来严重的后果，尤其对被解雇的员工及其家人而言。因此，我们应该尽可能避免这种情况。

The solution is to realize that natural selection, while inevitable, can be further pushed down to lower levels. Just like companies can protect themselves by firing their unfit employees, employees can protect themselves by firing their unfit mental patterns.

解决之道在于认识到，自然选择虽然不可避免，但可以进一步下推至更低的层级。正如公司可以通过解雇不称职的员工来保护自身一样，员工也可以通过摒弃不适应的思维模式来保护自己。

To protect the individual, natural selection must be free to act within the individual. There , it can select the beliefs and habits of his or hers that are fit (i.e., beneficial) and terminate those that are unfit (i.e., hinder their performance). 2

为了保护个体，自然选择必须在个体内部自由发挥作用。在那里，它可以选择个体中适合（即有益的）的信念和习惯，并淘汰那些不适合（即阻碍其表现的）信念和习惯。

# ↩

Fractalization

分形化

I call the process described above fractalization . The name comes from the realization that natural selection acts across levels with a fractal-like pattern. 3 Just as it acts within a market by selecting companies, it acts within companies selecting employees, within individuals selecting beliefs, and within beliefs selecting fragments.

我将上述过程称为分形化。这个名称源于这样一种认识：自然选择以类似分形的模式在不同层面发挥作用。正如它在市场中通过选择公司发挥作用一样，它也在公司内部通过选择员工发挥作用，在个人内部通过选择信仰发挥作用，并在信仰内部通过选择碎片发挥作用。

I mean it in the broadest sense possible. For example, species are made of individuals, and individuals of beliefs. By testing those beliefs against reality, and getting rid of false ones, one gets stronger and reduces his chances (and that of his population) of becoming the victim of natural selection. Similarly , markets are made of businesses, businesses of employees, and employees of beliefs and habits. 4

我的意思是尽可能广义地理解。例如，物种由个体组成，个体由信念组成。通过用现实检验这些信念，并摒弃错误的信念，个体就能变得更强大，并降低自身（以及其种群）成为自然选择牺牲品的几率。同样，市场由企业组成，企业由员工组成，员工则由信念和习惯组成。

Each level can protect itself from natural selection by becoming stronger. That requires letting natural selection work within itself. Natural selection is inevitable, but we can avoid it at any given level by pushing it towards a lower one (in some measure).

每个层级都可以通过自身变得更强大来抵御自然选择。这需要让自然选择在其内部发挥作用。自然选择不可避免，但我们可以通过（在某种程度上）将其推向更低的层级来避免在任何特定层级上受到自然选择的影响。

You , too, can take advantage of natural selection. Remember : whenever it encounters a population, it “kills” some of its members. Therefore , you can become stronger by considering yourself a population – of habits and beliefs – and getting rid of the unfit ones. Even though your ego wants to save them.

你也可以利用自然选择。记住：自然选择在面对一个群体时，总会“淘汰”一部分成员。因此，你可以把自己也看作一个群体——由习惯和信念构成——并剔除那些不适应环境的成员，从而变得更强大。即使你的本能想要保留它们。

People that consider their identity one and indivisible prevent natural selection from acting within them. Therefore , they do not grow stronger, and thus become vulnerable to natural selection acting on them.

那些将自身身份视为一体且不可分割的人，会阻碍自然选择在他们体内发挥作用。因此，他们无法变得更强大，从而更容易受到自然选择的影响。

If you want to survive, do not identify with your habits and beliefs but with their container. This way, you will let natural selection remove the habits and beliefs that are holding you down. You will get stronger and, thus, less likely to become the victim of natural selection yourself.

如果你想生存下去，不要认同你的习惯和信念，而要认同承载这些习惯和信念的载体。这样，你就能让自然选择剔除那些束缚你的习惯和信念。你会变得更强大，从而降低自己成为自然选择牺牲品的可能性。

( An additional point from Nassim Nicholas Taleb . “ As I have shown in Antifragile , the fragility of the components is required to ensure the solidity of the system. If humans were immortals, they would go extinct from an accident or a gradual buildup of misfitness. But shorter shelf life for humans allows genetic changes to accompany the variability in the environment.”)

（纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布补充一点：“正如我在《反脆弱》一书中阐述的，组成部分的脆弱性是确保系统稳固性的必要条件。如果人类是不朽的，他们最终会因为一次意外或逐渐积累的不适应而灭绝。但人类较短的寿命使得基因变化能够伴随环境的变异而发生。”）

# ↩

Example of a practical application

实际应用示例

As a teenager, I was shy. I had a lot of friends, but I would seldom ask girls out. If I did, I would do so in such an awkward way that they would refuse my invitation.

青少年时期，我很害羞。我有很多朋友，但我很少主动约女生。即使约了，我的方式也总是很笨拙，以至于她们都会拒绝我的邀请。

If my shyness continued, I could see myself becoming a victim of natural selection. I would end up alone and childless. Thankfully , I realized that the problem wasn’t my whole self but a part of me – my shyness. In particular, the problem was my mental beliefs that made me shy with girls. Once I realized that they were the problem, I could get rid of them. 5 I am now a confident man and married a wonderful woman.

如果我一直这么害羞，我感觉自己会成为自然选择的牺牲品，最终孤独终老，膝下无子。幸好，我意识到问题不在于我整个人，而在于我的一部分——我的害羞。具体来说，问题出在我那些让我面对女孩时感到羞怯的固有观念上。一旦我意识到这些观念才是问题的根源，我就能摆脱它们。如今，我自信满满，娶了一位贤惠的妻子。

1 Free markets are Petri dishes where experiments are continuously performed (new ventures), and the survivors decided by what works, not by what makes sense – this is the true engine of innovation.

1 自由市场就像培养皿，不断进行各种实验（新创企业），而最终的幸存者取决于什么有效，而不是什么有意义——这才是真正的创新引擎。

2 One caveat is over-adapting to temporary trends. There are three fundamental processes that prevent over-adaptation: alternating trying something new and seeing what works, a focus on both properties and data (never relying on either alone), and never taking bets that endanger the whole. None of these three processes are sufficient. You might find relevant my YouTube video “Proactive Metrics” (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AErgeP7dEU0).

2 需要注意的是，过度适应暂时的趋势是不可取的。有三个基本流程可以防止过度适应：不断尝试新事物并观察其效果；同时关注属性和数据（切勿单独依赖任何一方）；以及绝不冒险做出危及整体的事情。但这三个流程都不足以完全解决问题。您或许会对我在 YouTube 上的视频“主动指标”（https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AErgeP7dEU0）感兴趣。

3 “Fractal-like,” not “fractal.” I know well that the latter has a precise and restrictive meaning. Yet, I use here the terms “fractal-like” and “fractalization” as I found them very effective to convey an intuitive understanding of the phenomenon described in this chapter. As mentioned in the introduction, in the inevitable tradeoff between clarity and precision, I favor clarity.

3. 我用的是“类分形”，而不是“分形”。我深知后者含义精确且局限。然而，我在此使用“类分形”和“分形化”这两个术语，因为我发现它们能非常有效地传达对本章所述现象的直观理解。正如引言中所述，在清晰性和精确性之间不可避免地需要权衡，我更倾向于清晰性。

4 I arrived at this conclusion while thinking about antifragility (a concept described in Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s homonymous book). One of the three requirements for an entity to be antifragile is that it comprises elements that can be independently damaged. From there, I realized that making the monolithic a multitude is a major step towards antifragility.

4 我在思考反脆弱性（纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布在其同名著作中描述的概念）时得出了这个结论。一个实体具备反脆弱性的三个必要条件之一是它由可以独立受损的元素组成。由此，我意识到将单一整体分解为多个部分是迈向反脆弱性的重要一步。

5 We are extremely good at eliminating the beliefs that we acknowledge are the source of our problems once we realize that there is no alternative. Usually, this happens when we try everything else and still fail. Until then, getting rid of the mental patterns that are holding us back will be hard. Rather than doing that, we look for alternatives. Instead of removing, we add. Often, the opposite is better.

5. 一旦我们意识到别无选择，我们就会非常擅长消除那些我们承认是问题根源的信念。通常，这种情况发生在我们尝试了所有其他方法仍然失败之后。在此之前，摆脱那些阻碍我们前进的思维模式是件难事。我们不会这样做，而是寻找替代方案。我们不去去除，而是去添加。通常，反其道而行之反而更好。

SUMMARY OF THE FIRST STRATEGY, REDUCING EXPOSURE

第一项策略概述：降低风险敞口

T he first strategy to manage non-ergodicity is to reduce your exposure to irreversibility. In particular, we saw how:

应对非遍历性的首要策略是降低不可逆性风险。具体来说，我们已经了解了如何做到这一点：

– You can only optimize in reversible domains. Otherwise , you should first think about avoiding irreversibility.

——你只能在可逆域中进行优化。否则，你应该首先考虑避免不可逆性。

– You can reduce exposure to irreversibility by exposing only part of yourself (or of your assets, reputation, etc.). This is safer and more effective than going all-in on a medium-risk activity.

——你可以通过只投入部分自身（或资产、声誉等）来降低不可逆转的风险。这比孤注一掷地进行中等风险活动更安全、更有效。

It is safer to expose a bit of yourself to risk (to grab some upside) than not to do it. Otherwise , we involuntarily expose ourselves to the risks of inaction and obsolescence.

承担一些风险（以获取一些收益）比什么都不做要安全得多。否则，我们就会在不知不觉中让自己面临不作为和被时代淘汰的风险。

– An effective tactic consists of fractal systems and decreasing the ergodicity of the lower layers to increase that of the higher ones.

– 有效的策略是利用分形系统，降低底层遍历性，以提高高层遍历性。

– Nature gave us tools to manage non-ergodicity, in the form of moods and fear.

大自然赋予我们应对非遍历性的工具，即情绪和恐惧。

Here are a few ways in which you can apply the first strategy:

以下是应用第一种策略的几种方法：

– Invest your money as a barbell (most in low-downside assets, a bit in high-upside ones).

– 将资金像杠铃一样进行投资（大部分投资于下行风险较低的资产，少量投资于上行风险较高的资产）。

– Invest your time as a barbell (most in activities that strengthen your bedrock, a bit in explorative ones).

– 将你的时间投入到像杠铃一样的活动中（大部分时间投入到增强你基础的活动，少量时间投入到探索性的活动中）。

– Purposefully test your habits and beliefs to get rid of those that are negatively impacting your life or making you weak, while keeping an eye out for overoptimization to temporary trends.

有意识地检验你的习惯和信念，以摆脱那些对你的生活产生负面影响或使你变得软弱的习惯和信念，同时注意避免过度追求暂时的潮流。

The path forward

前进的道路

下一章将介绍管理非遍历性的第二种策略：利益攸关。

PART V

# ↩

ENSURE THAT THE DANGEROUS GETS REMOVED

确保清除危险物品

My favorite book of 2018 is Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s Skin In The Game .

我2018年最喜欢的书是纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布的《风险自负》。

My baker has skin in the game. If his bread is bad, he loses his reputation and clients. He might have to close his shop, eventually. In general, someone has skin in the game if, when wrong, they become the victim of their mistakes. Conversely , some managers can squeeze their team, make short-term decisions with catastrophic consequences, and then leave for another job position without suffering from the long-term consequences of their actions. They do not have skin in the game. ( Note that positive incentives, e.g., bonuses for achieving ambitious targets, do not give skin in the game because they incentivize excessive risk-taking; only incentives that provide sensitivity to losses give skin in the game).

我的面包师对此深有体会。如果他的面包不好，他就会失去声誉和顾客，最终可能不得不关门大吉。一般来说，如果一个人犯错后会成为自己错误的受害者，那么他才算是真正投入其中。相反，有些管理者可以压榨团队，做出一些会造成灾难性后果的短期决策，然后跳槽到其他岗位，而无需承担其行为的长期后果。他们并没有真正投入其中。（需要注意的是，积极的激励措施，例如，为实现远大目标而发放的奖金，并不能体现这种投入，因为它们会鼓励过度冒险；只有那些能够让员工对损失感同身受的激励措施才能体现这种投入。）

Skin in the game is of paramount importance because it protects populations and individuals. It does so in three ways. The following chapters describe them one by one.

利益攸关至关重要，因为它能保护群体和个人。它通过三种方式实现这一点。以下章节将逐一介绍这三种方式。

# ↩
29
# ↩

SKIN IN THE GAME REDUCES THE MORAL HAZARD

利益攸关降低道德风险

D ecision -makers who can make short-term decisions without being affected by their long-term consequences take excessive risks. This condition is called moral hazard.

那些能够做出短期决策而不考虑长期后果的决策者会承担过高的风险。这种情况被称为道德风险。

Moral hazard occurs when someone has incentives to increase an entity’s exposure to risk because he will not bear the full cost of that risk.

道德风险是指当某人有动机增加实体所面临的风险敞口，因为他不必承担该风险的全部成本时所发生的情况。

Other examples of moral hazards are parents imposing stressful career choices on their kids, politicians making decisions for regions they don’t live in, and unethical doctors suggesting unnecessary medical procedures.

道德风险的其他例子包括父母强迫孩子选择压力大的职业、政客为自己不居住的地区做决定，以及不道德的医生建议不必要的医疗程序。

The condition of suffering the consequences of one’s actions, “skin in the game,” is the opposite of moral hazard. It incentivizes people to make decisions that are good for them and others. As such, it helps protect populations.

承担自身行为后果，即“利益攸关”，与道德风险截然相反。它激励人们做出对自身和他人都有益的决定。因此，它有助于保护民众。

However , incentivization is not the only way skin in the game protects from harm. The next page shows another one.

然而，激励机制并非“利益攸关”保护自身免受伤害的唯一途径。下一页将介绍另一种途径。

# ↩
30
# ↩

SKIN IN THE GAME REMOVES SOURCES OF IRREVERSIBILITY

利益攸关消除了不可逆性的来源

D riving fines incentivize drivers not to exceed speed limits and avoid risky maneuvers that might endanger other cars. Yet , some drivers keep driving too fast and collecting fines. Part of the reason is that, for some drivers, fines are like fees. They are a cost that might be worth paying. 1

交通罚款旨在激励驾驶员不要超速行驶，避免可能危及其他车辆的危险驾驶行为。然而，一些驾驶员仍然超速行驶并收到罚款。部分原因是，对某些驾驶员来说，罚款就像费用一样，是值得支付的成本。

A single fine does not prevent the driver from driving again. If it were only for fines, drivers would be incentivized to drive slower but would not have skin in the game. Skin in the game requires more than just incentives.

一次罚款并不能阻止司机再次开车。如果只有罚款，司机虽然会受到激励而减速行驶，但却缺乏切身利益。而要真正承担责任，仅仅依靠激励是不够的。

Conversely , crashing stops a driver from driving again – either because he died or because the police canceled his driving license. It is not incentives that provide skin in the game, but irreversibility. 2

反之，车祸会让司机彻底失去驾驶资格——要么是因为死亡，要么是因为警方吊销了他的驾照。真正让人承担风险的不是激励机制，而是不可逆转的后果。

# ↩

Irreversibility, for whom?

不可逆性，对谁而言？

Irreversibility is not always bad. In a previous chapter, we saw that when we talk about irreversibility, we must specify the layer at which it takes place.

不可逆性并非总是坏事。在前一章中，我们看到，当我们谈论不可逆性时，必须具体说明它发生在哪个层面。

A dangerous criminal ending up in prison is bad for him but good for the upper layer: society. Similarly , a corrupt politician getting exposed and banned from public office is bad for him but good for society.

危险罪犯锒铛入狱对他本人不利，但对上层社会却有益。同样，腐败政客被揭露并被禁止担任公职，对他本人不利，但对社会却有益。

Populations want their members to have skin in the game. This way, over time, they get rid of those that expose themselves and others to risks.

民众希望成员们对自身利益负责。这样，随着时间的推移，他们就能清除那些让自己和他人身处险境的人。

# ↩

Populations, ergodicity, & skin in the game

人口、遍历性和利益攸关性

As we saw two pages ago, skin in the game requires irreversibility. Incentives that can be part of a cost-benefit analysis are not enough. A dangerous player might neglect them, whereas no one can neglect irreversibility.

正如我们在两页前看到的，利益攸关需要不可逆性。仅仅依靠成本效益分析的激励措施是不够的。危险的参与者可能会忽视这些激励措施，但没有人能够忽视不可逆性。

Moreover , as we saw on the last page, one member abandoning a population due to skin in the game benefits the population.

此外，正如我们在上一页所看到的，一个成员因为自身利益而放弃某个群体，反而有利于该群体。

Therefore , a population can decrease its exposure to irreversibility by exposing its members to it. Whether irreversibility has a positive or negative effect depends on the layer observed.

因此，群体可以通过让其成员接触不可逆因素来降低自身遭受不可逆因素的影响。不可逆因素的影响是积极的还是消极的，取决于所观察的层面。

# ↩

Limitations

局限性

Of course, this is only valid for exposures to irreversibility that do not have the potential to destroy a sizeable chunk of the population. Reckless drivers dying in car crashes do make cities safer, 3 for they disappear before they can hurt too many people, but inventors dying from creating an atomic bomb in their garage do not (though they probably do make the world safer by raising a concern and triggering a response to it – again, it depends on the scale considered).

当然，这仅适用于那些不可能导致大量人口死亡的不可逆事件。鲁莽驾驶者死于车祸确实会让城市更安全，因为他们在造成太多伤害之前就消失了；但发明家在自家车库里制造原子弹而丧命则不然（尽管他们可能通过引发关注并促使人们采取行动而让世界更安全——同样，这取决于所考虑的规模）。

# ↩

Summary of this chapter

本章概要

Skin in the game prevents dangerous individuals from hurting others. It does so in two ways. First , it incentivizes them not to do anything dangerous. Second , if they do, it prevents them from doing it again.

利益冲突机制可以防止危险分子伤害他人。它通过两种方式实现这一点。首先，它激励他们不要做任何危险的事情。其次，如果他们做了危险的事情，它能阻止他们再次作恶。

1 As a rule of thumb, we tend to neglect incentives that do not hit a bottleneck.

1. 按照经验，我们往往会忽略那些没有遇到瓶颈的激励措施。

2 In his book, Taleb makes the point that skin in the game is not about incentives but filtering.

2 在他的书中，塔勒布指出，利益攸关之处不在于激励，而在于筛选。

Also, it’s worth noting that some countries have a points-based driving license system, in which drivers lose points every time they break a law. This works fairly well but only partially counts as skin in the game, as not all drivers who drive dangerously are caught (and of those who do, in some countries, some can escape the penalty by declaring they weren’t the ones at the wheel and paying a higher fine).

此外，值得注意的是，一些国家实行积分制驾驶执照制度，驾驶员每次违法都会被扣分。这种制度运行良好，但其约束力有限，因为并非所有危险驾驶的驾驶员都会被抓到（而且在一些国家，即使被抓到，有些人也可以通过声称自己并非驾驶员并支付更高的罚款来逃避处罚）。

3 Given that dangerous drivers exist, we are better off with them disappearing sooner rather than later. Yes, we would be better off if dangerous drivers didn’t even begin driving, but that’s not realistic, not with the current transportation system.

3. 既然危险驾驶员确实存在，我们最好还是让他们早点消失。没错，如果危险驾驶员一开始就没有开车，那当然更好，但这并不现实，至少在目前的交通系统下是这样。

SKIN IN THE GAME PREVENTS DANGEROUS BEHAVIORS FROM SPREADING

风险承担能防止危险行为蔓延

I n the previous chapter, we saw how skin in the game prevents dangerous individuals from putting others in danger. This is not the only way skin in the game makes a population safer.

上一章我们看到，利益攸关如何阻止危险分子危害他人。但这并非利益攸关提升群体安全的唯一途径。

Take the example of frauds and charlatans. Most populations contain a few of them. In the absence of skin in the game, they can perpetuate their scam without consequences. They become famous. People imitate them instead of someone more competent. As a result, ineffective or dangerous behaviors spread. This is bad.

以骗子和江湖术士为例。大多数人群中都存在一些这样的人。由于他们无需承担任何风险，就能肆无忌惮地行骗。他们甚至会因此出名。人们会模仿他们，而不是去效仿那些更有能力的人。结果，无效甚至危险的行为蔓延开来。这很不好。

Conversely , in the presence of skin in the game, the success of charlatans is short-lived. Their mistakes cause them to leave the pool of celebrities people imitate before they influence the behavior of too many.

反之，一旦利益攸关，骗子的成功便会昙花一现。他们的错误会让他们从人们模仿的名人圈中消失，从而无法影响太多人的行为。

Skin in the game prevents dangerous or ineffective behaviors from spreading. It ensures that frauds, charlatans, and incompetents are quickly filtered out of the pool of experts that people imitate.

利益攸关能防止危险或无效的行为蔓延。它能确保骗子、江湖骗子和无能之辈迅速从人们效仿的专家群体中剔除出去。

On this topic, I recommend the following readings: “ Ergodicity and Digital Culture ,” 1 “ The Importance of Immediacy for Skin in The Game ,” 2 and “ Mimetic Societies .” 3

关于这个主题，我推荐以下阅读材料：《遍历性与数字文化》、《即时性对利益攸关的重要性》和《模仿社会》

1 The essay “Ergodicity and Digital Culture” (https://spearoflugh.substack.com/p/ergodicity-and-digital-culture-13ba17989890) makes the following point (here, paraphrased or quoted). In oral tradition, information spreads slowly, by word of mouth, from its practitioners. Information is filtered through time. Therefore, the behaviors that spread tend to be those that help with survival. In written tradition, information is filtered through the elites and the editors. [The information that survives tends to help with their survival.] Conversely, in “internet tradition,” spreading information is cheap and can be done instantaneously and by people without skin in the game. As a result, dangerous behaviors can easily spread wide. Culture building is non ergodic, for its spread through time yields different results than its spread through populations and digital culture achieves different results than oral tradition.

1. 论文《遍历性与数字文化》（https://spearoflugh.substack.com/p/ergodicity-and-digital-culture-13ba17989890）提出了以下观点（此处为意译或引用）：在口头传统中，信息通过口口相传，由实践者缓慢传播。信息会随着时间的推移而过滤。因此，传播开来的行为往往是那些有助于生存的行为。在书面传统中，信息会经过精英和编辑的过滤。[流传下来的信息往往有助于他们的生存。] 相反，在“互联网传统”中，信息的传播成本低廉，可以瞬间完成，而且传播者往往与事件本身并无直接利害关系。因此，危险的行为很容易广泛传播。文化建构并非遍历性的，因为其随时间传播的结果与随人口传播的结果不同，数字文化的结果也与口头传统不同。

2 As an example, contrary to common belief, many CEOs in the US and in many other countries do not appear to have skin in the game. Not in the short- and medium-term, at least – their violations and their companies’ go unpunished or yield fines that are similar to fees for bad behavior rather than limitations to conduct harmful business. This lack of effective immediate skin in the game coupled with their celebrity means that they become an attractive model whose behaviors to copy.

2 例如，与普遍认知相反，美国及其他许多国家的首席执行官似乎并未真正承担责任。至少在短期和中期内是如此——他们的违规行为及其公司往往逍遥法外，或者仅受到类似于不良行为罚款的处罚，而非对其有害商业行为的限制。这种缺乏直接责任感，加上他们的名人效应，使得他们成为人们争相效仿的榜样。

It is possible that these CEOs get criminally convicted at some point in the future. That doesn’t matter, for the purpose of behavioral imitation . If skin in the game materializes much more slowly than behaviors spreads, it is as if there were none.

这些CEO未来有可能被判刑事罪。但就行为模仿而言，这并不重要。如果利益冲突的发生速度远慢于行为的传播速度，那就如同利益冲突不存在一样。

What matters is not theoretical skin in the game. All entrepreneurs have it. Instead, what matters is if dangerous behaviors actually result in the entrepreneur losing his business or hitting some other form of game-over. If that doesn’t happen, or happens too slowly, then the dangerous behavior spreads well before its consequences materialize. It’s as if there wasn’t skin in the game, for the practical purposes at hand.

重要的并非理论上的利益冲突。所有创业者都身处其中。真正重要的是，危险行为是否真的会导致创业者失去企业或遭遇其他形式的失败。如果这种情况没有发生，或者发生得太慢，那么危险行为会在其后果显现之前就迅速蔓延开来。就实际情况而言，这就好比创业者根本没有利益冲突一样。

3 “Mimetic societies” is a short essay of mine freely available at bit.ly/mimeticsocieties

3 《模仿社会》是我撰写的一篇短文，可在 bit.ly/mimeticsocieties 免费获取。

SUMMARY OF THE SECOND STRATEGY, SKIN IN THE GAME

第二策略概要：切身利益

W e saw how:

我们看到了：

– Skin in the game acts as an incentive and as a filter that removes dangerous individuals from the community and prevents dangerous behaviors from spreading.

– 利益攸关既是一种激励，也是一种过滤器，可以将危险分子从社区中清除出去，防止危险行为的传播。

– Sociality helps align incentives within a community and conserve precious variance. It makes one feel like he cannot act against his community and then “jump ships.”

——社会性有助于协调社区内部的激励机制，并保存宝贵的差异性。它使人感到自己不能违背社区的意愿，然后“跳槽”。

Here are some practical applications:

以下是一些实际应用：

– Be wary of advice from people without skin in the game. They might be incompetent or not have your best interest at heart.

要警惕那些与此事没有直接利害关系的人的建议。他们可能能力不足，或者并非真心为你着想。

– Be wary of envying people without skin in the game. Imitating them might expose you to problems you didn’t consider.

——要警惕嫉妒那些没有切身利益的人。模仿他们可能会让你陷入意想不到的问题中。

– Be careful of removing social bonding from your life or organization in the name of efficiency: it has a purpose.

——不要为了提高效率而从你的生活或组织中消除社交联系：社交联系是有其存在的意义的。

PART VI
第六部分
# ↩

REDISTRIBUTION

再分配

In the second part of this book, we saw how Italian hospitals didn’t get very busy with COVID on average , yet some got overwhelmed. Systems can function well on average and yet fail locally.

本书第二部分提到，意大利各医院平均而言并未因新冠疫情而变得非常繁忙，但部分医院却不堪重负。医疗系统整体运行良好，但局部地区仍可能出现故障。

If the overwhelmed hospitals in Northern Italy could have instantaneously transferred the patients to the less busy ones of other regions, there would have been no difference between the local and the average. Each hospital would have been just as busy as any other one.

如果意大利北部不堪重负的医院能够立即将病人转移到其他地区不那么繁忙的医院，那么当地医院和平均水平的医院之间就不会有任何区别。每家医院的繁忙程度都会和其他医院一样。

However , in reality, hospitals cannot redistribute their patients fast enough. Hence the local failures.

然而，实际上，医院无法足够快地重新分配病人。因此才会出现局部地区的收治失败。

Redistribution influences whether a system working well on average also works well everywhere.

重新分配会影响一个平均运行良好的系统是否在任何地方都能良好运行。

A question worth asking is, “ When there is a local spike in load, can the system redistribute the load fast enough?” 1

值得探讨的问题是：“当局部负载出现峰值时，系统能否足够快地重新分配负载？”

This part of the book explains how redistribution helps manage non-ergodicity. The next chapter is about load redistribution, and the following one is about financial redistribution. You will learn how redistribution can help you, even if you’re better than those you redistribute with.

本书的这一部分解释了资源重分配如何帮助管理非遍历性。下一章将讨论负载重分配，再下一章将讨论财务重分配。您将了解到，即使您比与您进行资源重分配的对象更优秀，资源重分配也能帮助您。

An example: bulletproof jackets work by dispersing the load from the bullet hitting them across a large surface. If the hit load was restricted to a small area, it would pierce the clothing.

举例来说：防弹衣的工作原理是将子弹击中后产生的冲击力分散到更大的表面上。如果冲击力集中在一个小区域内，就会穿透衣物。

Incidentally , bulletproof jackets are made of Kevlar , a fiber created by chance by a DuPont researcher. In fact, of the four products that made DuPont’s fortune ( Nylon , Kevlar , Nomex , and Teflon ), two of them were discovered by chance while researching something else.

顺便一提，防弹衣是用凯夫拉纤维制成的，这种纤维是杜邦公司一位研究人员偶然发现的。事实上，杜邦公司赖以致富的四种产品（尼龙、凯夫拉、诺梅克斯和特氟龙）中，有两种都是在研究其他东西时偶然发现的。

1 A system that can redistribute load quickly is not immune to failure, just less likely. For example, a system that can perfectly redistribute growth will break once the load exceeds the number of load-bearing units times the unit’s load capacity. The slower the system can redistribute, the lower the number of load-bearing units and, thus, the lower the maximum load it can withstand.

1. 能够快速重新分配载荷的系统并非不会发生故障，只是发生故障的可能性较小。例如，一个能够完美重新分配增长的系统，一旦载荷超过承载单元的数量乘以每个单元的承载能力，就会发生故障。系统重新分配载荷的速度越慢，承载单元的数量就越少，因此，系统能够承受的最大载荷也就越低。
