LOAD REDISTRIBUTION

负载重新分配

I n the previous pages, we saw how hospitals would not have trouble managing local surges in hospitalization if they could instantaneously redistribute patients across all hospitals.

在前几页中，我们看到，如果医院能够立即将病人重新分配到所有医院，那么应对局部住院人数激增就不会有困难。

The faster a system can redistribute load, the more ergodic it is, all other things being equal. 1

在其他条件相同的情况下，系统重新分配负载的速度越快，其遍历性就越强。

This phenomenon applies to countries and large organizations, but also individuals. For example, the waiting room at my doctor’s was frequently overcrowded. He knew he had to do something. The expensive solution was to rent a larger studio with a larger waiting room. The smart solution was to take telephonic bookings. A booking system helps to redistribute loads (in this case, patients) over time.

这种现象不仅适用于国家和大型组织，也适用于个人。例如，我医生的候诊室经常人满为患。他知道必须采取措施。昂贵的解决方案是租用一个更大的诊室和候诊室。而明智的解决方案是接受电话预约。预约系统有助于在一段时间内重新分配就诊量（在本例中指患者）。

This is important. Spikes in load can cause irreversibility – for example, patients changing doctors because of too long waiting time (forever lost customers) and patients getting illnesses from staying too long in a crowded waiting room.

这一点很重要。就诊高峰可能会造成不可逆转的后果——例如，患者因为等待时间过长而更换医生（永远失去客户），以及患者因为在拥挤的候诊室待得太久而生病。

As another example, a good friend of mine recently purchased a car. He chose to pay it in monthly installments over five years. He did so even though he had the financial availability to pay it in cash. He explained that the loan allowed him to keep a buffer of money in the bank, to manage unexpected problems. If he paid the car cash and lost his job next month, he would be in dire straits.

再举个例子，我的一位好友最近买了辆车。他选择分五年按月分期付款。尽管他完全有能力一次性付清，但他还是选择了分期付款。他解释说，贷款让他可以在银行账户里留一些钱作为缓冲，以应对突发情况。如果他选择全款付清车款，而下个月又丢了工作，那他可就麻烦大了。

This makes sense! He decided to prioritize survival over optimization, the unexpected over the expected. Conversely , a clueless economist might call irrational the choice to pay something more when there is an option to pay it less. But temporal distribution matters.

这很有道理！他决定优先考虑生存而非优化，优先考虑意外而非预期。反过来，一个不懂行的经济学家可能会把明明可以选择少付钱却选择多付钱的行为称为不理性。但时间分布很重要。

Similarly , I’ve recently learned to appreciate actions that seem inefficient but increase my resilience to sudden spikes in load. For example, in the past, I tried to schedule all meetings in the city center on the same weekday, to minimize my travel time. Now , I try to spread them over two days. Yes , it means that I must commute twice. But it also allows me to benefit from unexpected events that would otherwise destroy my schedule, such as a client asking me to stay longer or a friend unexpectedly inviting me for lunch.

同样，我最近也学会了欣赏那些看似效率不高但却能增强我应对突发工作量激增能力的做法。例如，过去我总是尽量把所有在市中心的会议都安排在同一天，以减少通勤时间。现在，我尝试把会议分散到两天进行。没错，这意味着我要通勤两次。但这也让我能够从一些原本会打乱我计划的意外事件中获益，比如客户要求我加班，或者朋友突然邀请我共进午餐。

Pre -emptive redistribution increases resilience and opens up opportunities.

先发制人的资源再分配可以增强韧性并创造机会。

# ↩

Post-mortems and pre-mortems

死后尸检和死前尸检

In large organizations, when a project ends, it is common to conduct a post-mortem (it means “after-death”). This is a meeting in which the project manager and his team ask themselves, “ What went wrong? What should we do differently next time?”

在大型组织中，项目结束后通常会进行一次事后总结会议（简称“事后总结会议”）。在这次会议上，项目经理和他的团队会反思：“哪里出了问题？下次我们应该如何改进？”

Post -mortems bring precious insights. They are a useful practice. Even more useful are PRE -mortems . These are meetings held at the beginning of a project, in which the team asks, “ Let’s imagine that the project will have failed. What could have gone wrong? What actions should we take today to avoid this?”

事后分析能带来宝贵的见解，是一种很有用的做法。而事前分析则更有用。事前分析是在项目初期召开的会议，团队会在会上提出这样的问题：“假设项目失败了，可能出了什么问题？我们今天应该采取哪些措施来避免这种情况发生？”

Relying on post-mortems alone guarantees that you will be hit by some problems once. Conversely , pre-mortems give you a chance to avoid the problem before it gets a chance to hurt you. Post -mortems are reactive, whereas pre-mortems are proactive.

仅仅依靠事后分析，注定你会遭遇一些问题。相反，事前分析则能让你有机会在问题造成伤害之前就加以规避。事后分析是被动的，而事前分析是主动的。

Firefighters are essential, and yet a firefighting strategy that relies on reacting will have to fight more fires that it can attend to. The same applies to those relying on POST -mortems alone.

消防员至关重要，但依赖被动反应的消防策略最终将不得不应对超出其能力范围的火灾数量。仅仅依赖事后分析的策略也存在同样的问题。

Consider practicing pre-mortems for the important projects in your life. For example, before your vacation to the other side of the country, ask yourself, “ If this trip ended up in disaster, what could have caused it? Is there any preventive action I can take today?”

不妨对生活中重要的项目进行事前分析。例如，在你去外地度假之前，问问自己：“如果这次旅行以灾难告终，可能是什么原因造成的？我今天可以采取哪些预防措施？”

In particular – and here is where ergodicity and redistribution come into play – you could ask yourself the following question. “ Is there any moment of the vacation in which loads cluster together? Can I redistribute them?” For example, fatigue is a type of load. It might cluster during the 18-hour drive to the vacation spot. Falling asleep at the wheel or having a fight due to fatigue and stress are possible outcomes that might endanger the vacation and the relationship. The chances are that if something very bad happens during the holiday, it will happen where the load concentrates. A good idea might be to book an overnight stay mid-way, to redistribute the fatigue over two days.

尤其需要注意的是——这正是遍历性和重新分配发挥作用的地方——你可以问自己这样一个问题：“假期中是否存在某些环节，各种压力会集中出现？我能否重新分配这些压力？”例如，疲劳就是一种压力。它可能会在前往度假地的18小时车程中集中出现。开车时打瞌睡，或者因为疲劳和压力而发生争吵，都可能危及假期和彼此的关系。如果假期中真的发生了什么糟糕的事情，很可能就发生在压力集中的地方。一个好办法是在中途预订一晚住宿，将疲劳分散到两天内。

# ↩

Brittleness

脆性

Earlier , we saw how hospitals break down when there is a spike in patients and they cannot be redistributed to other hospitals.

之前我们已经看到，当病人数量激增且无法将病人重新分配到其他医院时，医院会不堪重负。

In mechanics, the inability to redistribute loads is called brittleness. Brittle materials, such as ceramics, break easily. This is because they cannot redistribute load spikes over their surface. A small hit, and they break. Conversely , ductile materials such as rubber and metal are more resistant. They can spread the load more evenly by deforming – something that ceramics cannot do. 2

在力学中，无法重新分配载荷的特性被称为脆性。脆性材料，例如陶瓷，很容易断裂。这是因为它们无法重新分配表面的载荷峰值。即使是轻微的冲击，它们也会断裂。相反，延性材料，例如橡胶和金属，则更耐用。它们可以通过变形更均匀地分散载荷——这是陶瓷无法做到的。

In general, deformation helps with survival. For example, if you are free to shift your schedule around, you are better able to resist sudden spikes in workload. Or , if your commute can “deform” to another route, you can avoid traffic jams.

一般来说，适应性强有助于生存。例如，如果你可以自由调整日程安排，就能更好地应对工作量的突然激增。或者，如果你的通勤路线可以“改变”成另一条路，就能避开交通拥堵。

As another example, Amazon Web Services is a multibillion-dollar business based on the idea of selling computers 3 that can “deform” and expand their computing capacity when they receive load above average.

再举一个例子，亚马逊网络服务 (AWS) 是一家价值数十亿美元的企业，其理念是销售计算机，当计算机接收到的负载超过平均水平时，这些计算机可以“变形”并扩展其计算能力。

The point is, to avoid breaking down, don’t be brittle. Deform to accommodate your loads. More importantly, do not make too many commitments that prevent you from deforming.

关键在于，为了避免损坏，不要过于脆弱。要能够变形以承受负荷。更重要的是，不要做出太多限制自身变形的承诺。

# ↩

Practical application

实际应用

As a freelancer, I learned that it is a good idea to keep some free time every week in case some overtime is required to meet a deadline. Otherwise , if something unexpected happens and I fail my deadline because I don’t have spare time to use, my client will be angry. He won’t give a damn if I have some free time next week.

作为一名自由职业者，我发现每周留出一些空闲时间非常重要，以防需要加班才能完成任务。否则，如果发生意外情况，导致我因为没有空闲时间而无法按时完成任务，客户会非常生气。他根本不会在意我下周是否有空闲时间。

It is not the average that matters, but the local. Local spikes require local buffers. 4

重要的不是平均值，而是局部值。局部峰值需要局部缓冲。

  1. Summary of this chapter
    本章概要

In this chapter, we have seen two concepts:

本章我们学习了两个概念：

– Redistributing loads helps prevent irreversible losses.

重新分配负荷有助于防止不可逆转的损失。

– Redistributing unexpected loads requires buffers or a local capacity to deform.

– 重新分配意外负载需要缓冲或局部变形能力。

1 For a hypothetical system that could redistribute load instantaneously, the local and the average would be the same, at least on the dimension of the particular load at hand.

1 对于一个可以瞬间重新分配负载的假想系统，局部和平均值将相同，至少在当前特定负载的维度上是如此。

2 What determines whether a material deforms or breaks under pressure is its capacity to redistribute load. It works like this. Imagine a ten-meter line on the ground, with ten dots, each one meter from the other. On each dot stands a person. They all form a line, holding hands. Now, take the largest dog you can find, and give the leash to one of the people. Finally, throw a piece of meat far away.

2. 决定材料在压力下是变形还是断裂的是它重新分配载荷的能力。原理是这样的：想象地面上有一条十米长的线，线上标有十个点，每个点之间相距一米。每个点上站着一个人。他们手拉手排成一列。现在，找一条你能找到的最大的狗，把狗绳交给其中一个人。最后，把一块肉远远地扔出去。

When the dog runs towards the meat, he will pull on the leash. The person holding it will be pulled too, and that person will begin pulling the people next to him. Two things might happen. First possibility, the other nine people prioritize staying on their dot. If the person with the leash pulls them away, they will release their hand, letting the dog carry that person away. The chain breaks. Second possibility, the other nine people don’t care about staying on their dots and focusing on holding hands together. They redistribute the force pulling on the leash between all of them, taking a few steps if needed. The chain doesn’t break.

当狗冲向肉的时候，它会拉扯牵引绳。牵绳的人也会被拉扯，然后这个人又会开始拉扯旁边的人。可能会出现两种情况。第一种情况是，其他九个人优先保持自己的位置。如果牵绳的人把他们拉走，他们会松开手，让狗带着牵绳的人跑开。这样，牵引绳就断了。第二种情况是，其他九个人不在乎是否保持自己的位置，而是专注于手拉手。他们会把拉扯牵引绳的力量分散到每个人身上，必要时会走几步。这样，牵引绳就不会断。

The first behavior – letting hands go rather than moving around and sharing the load – is what happens at a microscopic level in brittle materials, such as ceramics. Their grains (you can imagine them as groups of molecules) are stuck in a rigid structure. They cannot move around nor deform, and thus cannot effectively share load. A small hit is all it takes to break them. If your grandma’s ceramic vase falls from half a meter, it breaks.

第一种行为——放开双手而不是移动并分担重量——发生在脆性材料（例如陶瓷）的微观层面。它们的晶粒（你可以想象成分子群）被固定在一个刚性结构中。它们既不能移动也不能变形，因此无法有效地分担重量。只需轻轻一碰就会破碎。如果你奶奶的陶瓷花瓶从半米高的地方掉下来，它就会摔碎。

Conversely, the second behavior – moving around and sharing the load rather than letting hands go – is what happens at a microscopic level in ductile materials, such as metals. Their grains deform and share the load. It’s hard to break them. A metal bucket can fall from ten meters and not break.

相反，第二种行为——移动并分担负荷而不是松手——发生在延展性材料（例如金属）的微观层面。它们的晶粒会发生形变并分担负荷。它们很难被破坏。一个金属桶从十米高的地方掉下来也不会破碎。

3 Yes, it’s more complex than that, I know. But the true nature of AWS is beyond the scope of this book.

3 是的，我知道，情况比这复杂得多。但AWS的真正本质超出了本书的讨论范围。

4 Redistribution speed determines how far the buffer can be before it becomes useless.

4 重新分配速度决定了缓冲区在失效之前可以达到的最大容量。

Be particularly careful about situations in which redistribution speed is fast except during problems. For example, a healthcare system’s capacity to redistribute patients between hospitals slows down during a pandemic in which the ambulance staff gets sick.

要特别注意那些除了突发状况外，其他情况下医疗资源重新分配速度都很快的情况。例如，在疫情期间，如果救护人员生病，医疗系统在医院之间重新分配病人的能力就会下降。

FINANCIAL REDISTRIBUTION

金融再分配

M any people believe that redistribution of resources is something that helps the worst performers but also harms the best ones. This is true in an ergodic world. However , in a non-ergodic world, you can often benefit from redistribution, even if you’re giving more than you’re receiving. This phenomenon is so counterintuitive that I had to make a real-world example with numbers to believe in it myself.

许多人认为资源再分配有利于表现最差的人，却会损害表现最好的人。这在遍历性世界中确实如此。然而，在非遍历性世界中，即使你付出多于所得，你也常常能从资源再分配中获益。这种现象如此违反直觉，以至于我不得不举一个现实生活中的例子，用数字来佐证，才能相信它的存在。

Imagine that both you and your friend Aaron are offered the following game. You take turns shooting a basketball. If you make the basket, you double your money. If you fail, you halve it.

想象一下，你和你的朋友亚伦轮流投篮。如果投进，你的奖金翻倍；如果没投进，奖金减半。

You are a better player than Aaron . Whenever you shoot, you have a 60% chance to make it. Aaron has only a 50% chance. What’s the best strategy to maximize your gains (without caring about Aaron’s )?

你的球技比亚伦好。你每次投篮都有 60% 的命中率，而亚伦只有 50%。在不考虑亚伦的情况下，如何才能最大化你的收益？

Counterintuitively , if after both you and Aaron take a shot, the two of you decide to pool your money and take half each, you will end up with more money than if you decided to play by yourself – even if you are a better shooter than Aaron . 1

与直觉相反，如果你和亚伦都试射之后，决定把钱合在一起，一人一半，最终你得到的钱会比你单独玩的时候更多——即使你的枪法比亚伦好。

The next page explains why.

下一页将解释原因。

  1. Running the numbers
    计算结果

You start with $100. Imagine that you make the first shot and miss the second one. After the first shot (in), you double it to $200. After the second shot (out), you halve it to $100. You end up with the same money with which you began.

你一开始有100美元。假设你第一投进了，第二投没进。第一投（进）后，你的钱翻倍到200美元。第二投（出）后，你的钱减半到100美元。最终，你还剩下和开始时一样多的钱。

Now , let’s see what would have happened if you had played with Aaron and you had made the first shot while he missed his, and then you missed your second shot while he made his. You both made one shot in and one out. If , after each shot, you pooled your money and redistributed it half-half, the following happens.

现在，我们来看看如果你和亚伦一起玩，你第一杆进了，他没进，然后你第二杆没进，他进了，会发生什么。你们俩都各进一杆，各出一杆。如果每次打完球后，你们把钱集中起来，然后平分，就会出现以下情况。

You both begin with $100. After your first shot (in), you double your money to $200. After Aaron’s first shot (out), he halves his money to $50. The two of you then pool your money, for a total of $250, and divide it half-half. Now , you both have $125. After your second shot (out), you half your money to $62.5. After Aaron’s second shot (in), he doubles his money to $250. The two of you then pool your money, for a total of $312.5, and divide it half-half: you both have $156.25. The second scenario is much better for you than the first one! You end up with an extra $56.25!

你们俩一开始各有100美元。你第一次投篮命中后，你的钱翻了一番，变成200美元。亚伦第一次投篮命中后，他的钱减半，变成50美元。你们俩把钱凑在一起，总共250美元，然后平分。现在，你们俩各有125美元。你第二次投篮命中后，你的钱减半，变成62.5美元。亚伦第二次投篮命中后，他的钱翻了一番，变成250美元。你们俩把钱凑在一起，总共312.5美元，然后平分：你们俩各有156.25美元。第二种情况对你来说比第一种情况好得多！你最终多得了56.25美元！

( I know, it’s counterintuitive. I had to re-read the previous paragraph three times to convince me that it’s actually what’s going on.)

（我知道，这有悖常理。我不得不把上一段读了三遍才确信事情就是这样。）

This phenomenon occurs because when wins and losses are reciprocal multiples of the bet, the absolute amount won is higher than the absolute amount lost. It pays to redistribute, so that for each step forward, you only make a partial step back.

这种现象的出现是因为，当输赢金额是投注额的倒数倍时，赢的绝对金额会大于输的绝对金额。因此，重新分配资金是有利的，这样每向前迈进一步，你只会后退一部分。

# ↩

Redistributing pays even if you’re better

即使你能力更强，重新分配资源也是有利的。

The phenomenon described above holds even if you are a better shooter than the person with whom you pool your money. Let’s continue the experiment with you making the third shot, missing the fourth one, and making the fifth one, whereas Aaron does the opposite. In the end, three of your shots went in compared to two for Aaron : you shot better than him. In the scenario in which you do not redistribute, you end up with $200. If you redistribute, you end up with $305.

即使你的投篮技术比和你合伙投篮的人好，上述现象依然成立。我们继续这个实验：你投进了第三球，第四球没进，第五球投进了，而亚伦则相反。最终，你投进了三球，而亚伦只投进了两球：你的投篮技术比他好。如果不重新分配资金，你最终会得到 200 美元。如果重新分配资金，你最终会得到 305 美元。

Redistributing pays, even if you’re better than those with whom you redistribute. 2

即使你比那些与你一起分配资源的人更优秀，重新分配资源也是有利的。

Therefore , redistribution doesn’t only make sense from an ethical point of view but from a selfish one too.

因此，从伦理角度来看，重新分配财富是合理的，从自私的角度来看也是如此。

# ↩

Limitations and other considerations

局限性及其他考虑因素

There are some limitations to the previous statement. If Aaron were a terrible player, missing all his shots, then you would be better off without redistributing with him. Moreover , the thought experiment assumes that you do not spend your wealth between games and that your two performances are not correlated. If it were the case, when you missed, he would also be likely to miss, reducing the benefits of redistribution.

上述说法存在一些局限性。如果亚伦球技很差，投篮全失，那么你最好不要和他进行财富再分配。此外，这个假设假设你在两场比赛之间不会花费财富，并且你们两场比赛的表现没有相关性。如果情况确实如此，当你投篮不中时，他也很可能投篮不中，从而降低了财富再分配的益处。

Another consideration could be that a 50-50 split is inefficient, and perhaps a 60-40 could be more efficient. Splitting 50-50 might induce laziness. Incentives matter.

另一种考虑因素是，50/50 的分配效率低下，或许 60/40 的分配效率更高。50/50 的分配可能会导致员工懒惰。激励机制很重要。

That said, in general, some redistribution is better than no redistribution.

也就是说，总的来说，某种程度的财富再分配总比没有财富再分配要好。

# ↩

Redistribution increases ergodicity

重新分配提高了遍历性

The previous example showed how the problem with losses is not just that you lost something. It’s also that what you lost is no longer there to generate returns for you.

前面的例子表明，亏损的问题不仅仅在于你损失了某些东西，更在于你损失的那些东西再也无法为你带来收益。

For example, imagine you invested $1000 and lost $900 in a market downturn. When stocks double in price again, you will only end up with $200. The $900 you lost is no longer there to double its value to $1800.

例如，假设你投资了 1000 美元，在市场下跌时损失了 900 美元。当股价再次翻倍时，你最终只会剩下 200 美元。你损失的 900 美元已经无法再翻倍到 1800 美元了。

# ↩

Full and partial irreversibility

完全和部分不可逆性

There are two types of irreversibility.

不可逆性有两种类型。

The first one is what I call “game-over”: death, bankruptcy, and so on. These are points in your life’s trajectory that, when you touch them, you cannot leave ever again. This irreversibility is total.

第一种是我所谓的“游戏结束”：死亡、破产等等。这些是你人生轨迹上的点，一旦触及，就再也无法回头。这种不可逆转性是彻底的。

The second type of irreversibility is partial. Some situations impair you and make recovery hard but not impossible or cap your full potential while allowing for partial recovery. For example, investing losses that do not cause bankruptcy, an injury that lets you exercise but not quite like before, and so on.

第二种不可逆性是部分不可逆的。有些情况会损害你的能力，使康复变得困难，但并非不可能，或者限制你的全部潜能，但仍允许部分康复。例如，投资损失不会导致破产，受伤后可以锻炼但不如以前那么剧烈，等等。

Redistribution helps mitigate both types of irreversibility. For example, unemployment benefits help avoid personal bankruptcy. The redistribution scheme in the basketball example above helps avoid excessive losses that are difficult to recoup.

再分配有助于减轻这两种类型的不可逆性。例如，失业救济金有助于避免个人破产。上述篮球例子中的再分配方案有助于避免难以弥补的巨额损失。

Since irreversibility causes non-ergodicity, we can say that redistribution helps to decrease non-ergodicity.

由于不可逆性导致非遍历性，我们可以说重新分配有助于减少非遍历性。

As a reminder, in this book, I refer to ergodicity as a non-binary property. This is because of the practical reasons explained in Part 3.

再次提醒，本书中我将遍历性视为一种非二元属性。这是因为第三部分会解释一些实际原因。

# ↩

Practical applications

实际应用

Here are some practical applications of redistribution:

以下是一些重新分配的实际应用：

– Taxes , obviously, but also other voluntary forms of financial redistribution within tight communities, such as shared pools of money. 3 Also , insurance and debt.

– 税收当然是其中之一，但紧密社区内的其他自愿性金融再分配形式，例如共享资金池，也是其中之一。此外，还有保险和债务。

– Social ties are, in a way, a form of redistribution of time and care. I give you some of my time when I do not need it. In exchange, I get a chance to use some of your time when I need it.

从某种意义上说，社会关系是一种时间和关爱的重新分配。我不需要的时候会把时间给你，作为交换，我需要的时候也可以利用你的时间。

– Rebalancing a portfolio, sharing knowledge, playing positive-sum games, and reinvesting part of your finances in your community are forms of redistribution. They help build direct and indirect safety nets that might benefit you in case your fortune changes.

——重新平衡投资组合、分享知识、参与正和博弈以及将部分资金再投资于社区都是财富再分配的形式。它们有助于建立直接和间接的安全网，在你财富发生变化时，这些安全网可能会使你受益。

# ↩

Rebalancing a portfolio

重新平衡投资组合

A few more words on this last topic. There are tech employees who have most of their wealth in the form of very valuable stock options in the company they work for. They know about the importance of redistribution but don’t redistribute their assets because “there’s nothing they could buy with a higher expected value of their stock options.”

关于最后一个话题，我再补充几句。有些科技公司的员工，他们的大部分财富都以所在公司价值极高的股票期权的形式存在。他们知道资产再分配的重要性，但却不愿进行再分配，因为他们认为“没有任何东西能比这些股票期权的预期价值更高”。

Let’s assume they are correct and the company they work for has a 50% chance of becoming the next Google . That would still not be a good reason not to redistribute. That’s because, while they would have a significant chance at becoming multi-millionaires, they would also have a significant chance at their options becoming worthless. Conversely , if they diversified half of their wealth into, say, a mix of bonds and stocks, they would still retain a significant chance at becoming multi-millionaires (though less “multi” than before) and would end up very wealthy in 100% of the cases (because of the stocks and bonds).

假设他们的判断是正确的，他们所在的公司有50%的概率成为下一个谷歌。但这仍然不是不进行资产再分配的好理由。因为，虽然他们很有可能成为千万富翁，但他们的期权也很有可能变得一文不值。相反，如果他们将一半的财富分散投资到债券和股票的组合中，他们仍然有很大概率成为千万富翁（虽然概率不如以前那么高），而且100%的情况下都会非常富有（因为股票和债券的收益）。

While the expected average outcome of the second solution might be lower than the first one, it has a better distribution of outcomes: instead of leading to huge wealth in some scenarios, it leads to huge wealth in any scenario.

虽然第二个方案的预期平均结果可能低于第一个方案，但它的结果分布更好：它不是在某些情况下带来巨额财富，而是在任何情况下都带来巨额财富。

Comparing average outcomes misses a benefit of redistribution: a better distribution of outcomes. In other words, it makes your happiness more certain.

比较平均结果忽略了财富再分配的一项益处：更合理的结果分配。换句话说，它能让你更确定地获得幸福。

# ↩

Insurance

保险

In their Ergodicity Economics , 4 Ole Peters and Alexander Adamou show that insurance is a puzzle that expected values alone cannot solve.

在他们的遍历性经济学中，奥勒·彼得斯和亚历山大·阿达穆表明，保险是一个仅靠期望值无法解决的难题。

Let’s say you have a house worth $100,000 and that there is a 1% possibility of it being burned down any given year. You are considering whether to buy insurance that would give you back the value of your house ($100,000) in case it burns down.

假设你拥有一栋价值 10 万美元的房子，并且每年有 1% 的概率会被烧毁。你正在考虑是否购买保险，以便在房子被烧毁时获得房屋价值（10 万美元）的赔偿。

The expected yearly value of the insurance contract would be the value of the insured good ($100,000) multiplied by the chance of the insurance triggering (1%). The total is $1000.

该保险合同的预期年价值为被保险货物的价值（10万美元）乘以保险触发概率（1%），总计1000美元。

The insurer would want more than $1000 to cover his operating costs. In contrast, the owner would be willing to pay $1000 at most. Since these two ranges do not overlap – more than $1000, and up to $1000 – we would expect insurance contracts never to be signed. In reality, they are common. So , something else must be going on.

保险公司会要求超过 1000 美元的赔偿金来支付运营成本。相比之下，车主最多只愿意支付 1000 美元。由于这两个范围互不重叠——超过 1000 美元和不超过 1000 美元——我们原本以为保险合同根本不会签订。但实际上，这类合同却很常见。所以，这背后肯定另有隐情。

Not insuring one’s house means that a fire might cause its owner to go bankrupt. In contrast, a single house taking fire doesn’t cause its insurer to go bankrupt.

不给房屋投保意味着一旦发生火灾，房主可能会破产。相反，一栋房屋发生火灾并不会导致保险公司破产。

Therefore , the owner is willing to pay a premium to protect themselves from irreversibility. The insurer is willing to sell this protection from irreversibility because it increases their own exposure less than it decreases it for the owner. This is because the insurer is wealthier than the house owner and can thus tolerate larger temporary losses without going bankrupt. 5

因此，业主愿意支付保费来规避不可逆转的风险。保险公司也愿意出售这种不可逆转风险保障，因为它增加自身风险的幅度小于降低业主风险的幅度。这是因为保险公司比业主财力雄厚，因此能够承受更大的暂时性损失而不会破产。

# ↩

Additional notes on insurances

关于保险的补充说明

I simplified the previous example a lot. Ole Peters and Alexander Adamou offer a detailed and formal explanation in their paper “ Ergodicity Economics . ”

我大幅简化了前面的例子。Ole Peters 和 Alexander Adamou 在他们的论文《遍历性经济学》中提供了详细而正式的解释。

Another way to grasp what is going on is to remember that (non)ergodicity is not just a property of an activity – in this case, insurance. Instead , it is a property of an actor, an activity, and the exposure of the former to the latter. Hence , the same activity might affect differently the ergodicity of two different actors. Any analysis claiming irrationality without considering this point is likely to be flawed.

另一种理解问题的方法是记住，（非）遍历性不仅仅是某项活动（在本例中为保险）的属性。相反，它是行为主体、活动以及前者对后者的影响的属性。因此，同一项活动可能对两个不同行为主体的遍历性产生不同的影响。任何不考虑这一点就声称存在非理性行为的分析都可能是有缺陷的。

# ↩

Other benefits of redistribution

再分配的其他好处

So far, we have only seen the direct benefits of redistribution. There are indirect ones too. For example, it eases social tension, creates a stabler system, and fosters positive-sum games (in the previous example, it incentivizes me to teach Aaron to shoot better, and incentivizes Aaron to give me feedback that might improve my skills and, therefore, our returns).

到目前为止，我们看到的只是财富再分配的直接好处。其实它也有间接好处。例如，它可以缓解社会紧张局势，创造更稳定的体系，并促进正和博弈（在前面的例子中，它激励我教亚伦提高射击水平，也激励亚伦给我反馈，从而提高我的技能，进而提高我们的收益）。

# ↩

Altruism and redistribution

利他主义和再分配

As we saw in the previous pages, redistribution has many benefits. I suspect that we evolved altruism to produce redistributive behaviors that indirectly benefit us.

正如我们在前几页所看到的，再分配有很多好处。我怀疑我们进化出利他主义是为了产生那些间接使我们受益的再分配行为。

# ↩

Localism and its benefits

地方主义及其益处

In a centralized country, decisions are taken by institutions at the country’s geographical, cultural, and social center. These decisions are then applied equally to the whole country, with no tailoring.

在中央集权国家，决策由位于国家地理、文化和社会中心的机构制定。这些决策随后会平等地适用于全国，不作任何调整。

Conversely , localism (the opposite of centralization) wants decision-making to happen at the lowest level possible – at the community level, if possible; if not, at the town level; if not, at the province level, and so on. This allows the decision-makers to know the topic of the decision closely, to have skin in the game so that they do not take excessive or unethical risks, and to make very tailored policies. These are very valuable benefits, particularly in the long term, because they make mistakes less likely.

相反，地方主义（与中央集权相反）主张决策尽可能在最低层级进行——如果可能，在社区层面；如果不行，则在城镇层面；如果城镇也行，则在省级层面，以此类推。这使得决策者能够深入了解决策主题，切身参与决策过程，从而避免承担过大或不道德的风险，并制定更具针对性的政策。这些优势非常宝贵，尤其从长远来看，因为它们能降低出错的概率。

# ↩

Variance benefits ergodicity

方差有利于遍历性

On the one hand, we saw how populations benefit from the action of natural selection on some of their members. 6 On the other hand, populations want most of their members to survive, not just their fitter ones. This is for three reasons. One , we are humans. Two , numbers bring strength. Three , numbers bring variance, and variance is important.

一方面，我们看到种群如何从自然选择对部分成员的作用中获益。另一方面，种群希望大多数成员都能生存下来，而不仅仅是那些更适应环境的成员。这有三个原因。第一，我们是人类。第二，数量带来力量。第三，数量带来变异，而变异至关重要。

As environments change and predators or competitors evolve, the traits required for thriving vary too. One day, the tribe might need someone strong. Another day, it might need someone smart. It is wise to preserve the smart even when their skills are not needed. 7

随着环境变化和捕食者或竞争对手的进化，生存所需的特质也会随之改变。有时，部落需要强壮的人；有时，则需要聪明的人。即使不再需要他们的技能，明智的做法也是保留聪明的人。

Altruism and redistribution help to keep a population diverse and thus more resistant to the unknowns of the future. 8

利他主义和财富再分配有助于保持人口多样性，从而增强其抵御未来未知风险的能力。

1 This is an adaptation from the famous “Farmer’s Fable” thought experiment. The reason for the adaptation is that, in the fable, the two farmers have the same payoffs. Here, I wanted to show that even when one participant has higher payoffs than the others, it often pays to redistribute anyway.

1 这是对著名的“农夫寓言”思想实验的改编。之所以进行改编，是因为在原寓言中，两位农夫的收益相同。而在这里，我想表明，即使一位参与者的收益高于其他参与者，重新分配收益通常也是有益的。

2 Up to a limit, of course (which depends on the odds, the payoffs, and the time horizon), but it’s a much higher limit than I would have intuitively thought. More on these limitations will be discussed on the next page.

2 当然，这并非绝对（取决于赔率、收益和时间跨度），但这个上限远比我直觉上想象的要高。关于这些限制的更多内容将在下一页讨论。

3 Note that unemployment benefits and public healthcare would fit in this category but not pensions and other retirement benefits – they are not a method to help individuals withstand short-term irreversibility.

3 请注意，失业救济金和公共医疗保健属于此类，但养老金和其他退休福利不属于此类——它们不是帮助个人抵御短期不可逆转性的方法。

4 https://ergodicityeconomics.files.wordpress.com/2018/06/ergodicity_economics.pdf

4 https://ergodicityeconomics.files.wordpress.com/2018/06/ergodicity_economics.pdf

5 Peters and Adamou explain it as insurance allowing for higher time-average growth rates despite appearing to be the purchase of an expected loss.

5 Peters 和 Adamou 将其解释为一种保险，允许更高的平均增长率，尽管表面上看起来像是购买预期损失。

6 Or components.

6 或其组成部分。

7 On a related note, a major problem I see in the governments of some countries is a lack of variance.

7 顺便提一下，我认为一些国家政府的一个主要问题是缺乏多样性。

8 In centralization, redistribution follows the pattern: local → central → local. For example, my taxes go to the central government, which redistributes it to the regions, which redistribute it to the provinces, and so on. Conversely, in localism, redistribution follows the arc: local → local, at least for the most part. For example, part of my taxes goes to my town, which uses them for initiatives that improve my town and the lives of its citizens.

8. 在中央集权体制下，资源再分配遵循“地方→中央→地方”的模式。例如，我的税款上缴中央政府，中央政府再将其分配给各地区，各地区再分配给各省，以此类推。相反，在地方自治体制下，资源再分配遵循“地方→地方”的模式，至少在大多数情况下如此。例如，我的一部分税款拨给我所在的城镇，城镇将其用于改善城镇及其居民生活的各项举措。

This is good: someone who knows that his money will go to his town knows that he will benefit indirectly from his contribution. Therefore, he is more likely to contribute and might contribute more, further increasing the benefits for his community and for him.

这很好：如果一个人知道自己的捐款会用于他所在的城镇，他就会知道自己会间接受益。因此，他更有可能捐款，而且可能会捐更多，从而进一步增加社区和他自身的收益。

This is not to say that redistribution should only happen locally. For some risks, redistribution is more effective at higher scales. For example, regions affected by an earthquake might benefit from the operational and financial help of other less-affected regions.

这并非意味着资源再分配只能在局部范围内进行。对于某些风险而言，更大范围的资源再分配更为有效。例如，受地震影响的地区或许能够从其他受灾较轻的地区获得运营和财政援助。

# ↩

ERGODICITY, COOPERATION, AND EVOLUTION

遍历性、合作与演化

S haring resources can be beneficial. In the basketball example contained in the previous chapter, I showed how some degree of redistribution benefits even top performers – i.e., those giving more than they receive. As a reminder, the example consisted of you and another person taking turns shooting a free throw. Making a free throw doubles your money, but missing it halves it. Suppose you are a better shooter and have a 60% chance of making the shot, whereas the other shooter has only a 50% chance. I ran the numbers and showed that if players share part of their gains after each shot, not only do the worst shooters amass more money compared to the scenario in which there is no redistribution, but also the better ones end up better off. This is because, in multiplicative systems, even though the top performers share more than they give, smoothening their losses increases their wealth’s growth rate.

资源共享是有益的。在前一章的篮球例子中，我展示了一定程度的资源再分配如何使顶尖球员——即那些付出多于所得的人——受益。回顾一下，这个例子是你和另一个人轮流罚球。罚中一球，你的奖金翻倍；罚不中，奖金减半。假设你的投篮命中率更高，有 60% 的命中率，而另一个球员只有 50%。我计算了一下，如果球员在每次投篮后分享一部分收益，不仅投篮最差的球员最终会比不进行资源再分配的情况下积累更多财富，而且投篮最好的球员最终也会受益。这是因为，在乘法系统中，即使顶尖球员分享的比付出的多，通过平减损失也能提高他们的财富增长率。

In May 2022, one and a half years after the first edition of this book was published, Ole Peters and Alexander Adamou published a new paper (“ The ergodicity solution of the cooperation puzzle”), further exploring resource redistribution. Though very technical, it’s also very interesting, so I took the freedom to explain and discuss some of its findings.

2022年5月，在本书第一版出版一年半之后，奥勒·彼得斯和亚历山大·亚当穆发表了一篇新论文《合作难题的遍历性解决方案》，进一步探讨了资源再分配问题。尽管内容非常技术性，但也十分引人入胜，因此我决定在此解释和讨论其中的一些发现。

# ↩

Why do people cooperate?

人们为什么会合作？

Peter’s and Adamou’s paper begins with the question, “ Why do people cooperate by sharing resources?”

Peter 和 Adamou 的论文以“人们为什么通过共享资源进行合作？”这个问题开篇。

Common answers include reciprocity (“ I help you today, so you help me tomorrow”) and specialization (“ I share my food, and you share your tools”). These are valid benefits of sharing. However , the paper adds that sharing is beneficial even in the absence of reciprocity and specialization.

常见的答案包括互惠（“我今天帮你，你明天帮我”）和分工（“我分享食物，你分享工具”）。这些都是分享带来的益处。然而，该论文补充说，即使没有互惠和分工，分享仍然是有益的。

This is because, in a volatile world, cooperation increases growth by reducing the irreversible losses caused by volatility. It smoothens losses so that an adverse event is less likely to cause a game over. Moreover , when growth is back, you have more resources left and can, therefore, capture more of that growth.

这是因为，在动荡的世界中，合作能够减少波动造成的不可逆转损失，从而促进增长。它能平滑损失，降低不利事件导致经济崩溃的可能性。此外，当经济增长恢复时，你将拥有更多资源，因此可以抓住更多增长机遇。

The paper offers solid mathematical demonstrations, but consider the following simple example. Imagine you and I are hunters, and we do not share food. If you undergo a series of unfortunate “no catches,” you might starve and die. Conversely , if we share part of our catches, we reduce the chances of either one of us dying. Not only do we become stronger than the sum of the parts, but each of the parts selfishly benefits too. Even the one that shares more than they receive.

论文提供了严谨的数学论证，但请考虑以下简单的例子。假设你我都是猎人，我们不分享食物。如果你连续几次空手而归，你可能会饿死。相反，如果我们分享一部分猎物，就能降低我们彼此死亡的概率。这样一来，我们不仅整体实力大于个体之和，而且每个人都能从中受益，即使是分享多于所得的那一方也不例外。

This is the advantage of cooperation: it reduces the likelihood of losses that absorb future gains.

这就是合作的优势：它降低了损失的可能性，从而避免了未来收益的损失。

# ↩

Risk Management

风险管理

One sentence from the paper stayed with me: “ Good risk management does not merely reduce the size of […] down-swings. It also improves long-time performance.” I made this point in previous chapters of the book, but it’s worth repeating. Limiting losses is not just a strategy to decrease adverse risk; it is also a chance to increase opportunities and our ability to capitalize on them.

论文中有一句话让我印象深刻：“良好的风险管理不仅仅能减少下跌的幅度，还能提升长期业绩。”我在本书的前几章中也提到过这一点，但值得再次强调。限制损失不仅仅是降低不利风险的策略，它还能增加机遇，并提升我们把握机遇的能力。

Hence , risk management should be part of any organization and society’s core governance and not just be relegated to a side committee with limited influence. Each of the company’s top leaders should have, in their job description, a focus on managing risk to improve long-term growth by reducing irreversible losses – financial and non. For example, consider employee turnover. If an employee quits your company, the cost is not just the time, effort, and sign-on fees to replace them. It is also that whatever skills, knowledge, and relationships the employee accrued and could have produced returns are now gone.

因此，风险管理应当成为任何组织和社会的核心治理组成部分，而不应仅仅被置于影响力有限的附属委员会之下。公司的每一位高层领导都应在其职责范围内，重点关注风险管理，以减少不可逆转的损失（包括财务损失和非财务损失），从而促进长期增长。例如，考虑员工流动。如果一名员工离职，成本不仅仅是招聘替代者所需的时间、精力和签约费用，还包括该员工积累的技能、知识和人脉关系，这些原本可以为公司带来收益，如今也随之消失。

Hence , the importance of considering growth maximization, the objective of many companies, as consisting not just of the acquisition of new resources but also the protection of the existing ones – because the latter is needed to capture the former. 1

因此，许多公司追求的增长最大化不仅包括获取新资源，还包括保护现有资源——因为后者是获取前者的必要条件。

# ↩

Natural selection

自然选择

Another critical point of Peters ’ and Adamou’s paper regards evolution. Animals , including us, are multicellular organisms. The benefits of multicellularity are evident: it enables specialized organs, such as legs and brains. However , we didn’t directly evolve from single-cell to million-cell organisms. Before that, there probably were two-cell organisms. And what’s the benefit of that?

彼得斯和阿达穆论文的另一个关键点涉及进化。包括我们人类在内的动物都是多细胞生物。多细胞性的优势显而易见：它使我们能够拥有专门的器官，例如腿和大脑。然而，我们并非直接从单细胞生物进化到百万细胞生物。在此之前，可能存在双细胞生物。那么，双细胞生物的优势是什么呢？

On the one hand, two cells are too few to enable specialization. On the other hand, it must have some benefit; otherwise, natural selection would not have selected such an organism. Sharing resources, thus enabling survival in downturns, could be one of such benefits.

一方面，两个细胞太少，不足以实现细胞分化。另一方面，细胞分化必然有其益处；否则，自然选择不会选择这样的生物体。共享资源，从而在资源匮乏时期得以生存，可能就是这种益处之一。

The same applies to societies: a tribe whose members share resources is more likely to survive a famine. But , and here is the paper’s key point, we do not need group selection to explain why we evolved the tendency to share resources. As explained at the beginning of this chapter, moderate sharing also benefits the individual. Individuals who participate in sharing are more likely to survive. Hence , individual selection is enough to explain why we evolved a tendency to share resources.

这同样适用于社会：一个部落如果成员之间共享资源，就更有可能在饥荒中幸存下来。但是，本文的关键在于，我们并不需要群体选择来解释我们为何进化出共享资源的倾向。正如本章开头所述，适度的共享对个体也有益处。参与共享的个体更有可能生存下来。因此，个体选择足以解释我们为何进化出共享资源的倾向。

In the words of the paper, “individuals poll and share resources because, over a temporal sequence of interactions, it is individually advantageous for them to do so […] group selection is not needed [to explain sharing] because the interests of the group and individual are aligned.” And then, “cooperation […] is advantageous for the simple reason that those who do it outgrow those who do not.”

正如论文中所述，“个人之所以会征集和分享资源，是因为在一系列互动中，这样做对他们个人有利[…]无需群体选择[来解释分享行为]，因为群体和个人的利益是一致的。” 然后，“合作[…]之所以有利，原因很简单：合作者会超越不合作者。”

# ↩

Why don’t we cooperate?

我们为什么不合作？

After reading the paper, I wondered, “ If cooperation and resource sharing are so important, why don’t we do them more?”

读完这篇论文后，我不禁思考：“如果合作和资源共享如此重要，为什么我们不更多地进行合作和资源共享呢？”

Part of the answer is that while some degree of resource sharing is beneficial, full sharing is probably harmful or at least suboptimal. Country -wide communist experiments show that we do not want bad performers, such as a company producing subpar appliances, to grow at the same rate as good performers. Instead , we want good performers to grow faster than bad performers so that more resources are diverted to those having demonstrated a higher ability to put them to good use.

部分答案在于，虽然一定程度的资源共享是有益的，但完全共享可能有害，或者至少并非最优。全国范围的共产主义实验表明，我们不希望表现不佳的企业（例如生产劣质家电的公司）与表现良好的企业以相同的速度增长。相反，我们希望表现良好的企业比表现不佳的企业增长得更快，这样就能将更多资源分配给那些展现出更高资源利用能力的企业。

Another part of the answer is that not sharing appears beneficial to the individual. That tempts us to defect (for example, by evading taxes while still benefiting from the redistribution from those who do pay them). That said, defection is only apparently beneficial to the individual. The reason is that if you are the only one evading taxes, you are probably better off evading them. But if too many people evade them, you are worse off because you lose the redistribution effect that this chapter showed to be essential. Same thing if you slack off at work or refuse to help your colleagues. If you could do it in a vacuum, great. But in real life, doing it increases the chances of everyone else doing it, and soon enough, you find yourself in an unproductive team that gets laid off or in a company that doesn’t make enough money to pay decent salaries.

答案的另一部分在于，不分享似乎对个人有利。这会诱使我们背叛（例如，通过逃税来继续享受那些纳税人带来的财富再分配）。也就是说，背叛对个人的益处只是表面上的。原因在于，如果你是唯一一个逃税的人，那么逃税可能对你更有利。但如果太多人逃税，你的处境就会更糟，因为你失去了本章所阐述的至关重要的财富再分配效应。如果你在工作中偷懒或拒绝帮助同事，情况也是如此。如果你能独自这样做，那当然很好。但在现实生活中，这样做会增加其他人效仿的可能性，很快，你就会发现自己身处一个效率低下的团队，最终被裁员，或者身处一家无法支付体面薪水的公司。

Chapter summary

章节概要

Ergodicity is sufficient to demonstrate that cooperation by sharing resources brings benefits not only to collectives but also to individuals. It hence explains why individuals who share got selected over those who don’t, and thus why we developed altruism and similar cooperative tendencies.

遍历性足以证明，通过资源共享进行合作不仅对集体有益，对个人也有益。因此，它解释了为什么乐于分享的人比不愿分享的人更容易被选中，以及为什么我们会发展出利他主义和类似的合作倾向。

我的咨询业务重点之一是风险管理如何促进组织发展。如果您想了解更多信息，请给我发邮件。

SUMMARY OF THE THIRD STRATEGY, REDISTRIBUTION

第三项策略（再分配）概述

W e saw that some degree of redistribution within a system increases the ergodicity of its participants. 1

我们发现，系统内部一定程度的重新分配会提高参与者的遍历性。

We also learned that in load distribution, the capacity to deform (i.e., redistribute load) allows the mitigation of load spikes that are often the trigger for irreversible damage.

我们还了解到，在载荷分布中，变形能力（即重新分配载荷）可以减轻载荷峰值，而载荷峰值通常是造成不可逆损坏的触发因素。

Finally , we saw how redistribution not only helps to avoid gameovers but also increases long-term outcomes, even for those who are more effective than the average person.

最后，我们看到，重新分配不仅有助于避免游戏结束，而且可以提高长期收益，即使对于那些比普通人更有效率的人来说也是如此。

1 There are exceptions. For example, extreme redistribution might cause incentive problems, moral hazards, or tragedies of the common. However, in general, some redistribution is beneficial.

1. 当然也有例外。例如，极端的财富再分配可能会导致激励机制失灵、道德风险或公地悲剧。然而，总的来说，适度的财富再分配是有益的。

PART VII
第七部分
# ↩

LUCK & SKILL

运气与技巧

Nassim Taleb recently wrote: 1 “ Elon Musk illustrates my point made in Fooled by Randomness : solid financial success is largely the result of skills, hard work, and wisdom. But wild success is more likely to be the result of reckless betting, extreme luck, and the opposite of wisdom: folly.”

纳西姆·塔勒布最近写道： 1 “埃隆·马斯克印证了我在《随机漫步的傻瓜》一书中提出的观点：稳健的财务成功很大程度上源于技能、努力和智慧。但巨大的成功更有可能是鲁莽的赌博、极好的运气以及与智慧相反的愚蠢行为的结果。”

First of all, let me clarify that I agree both with Taleb (much of Musk’s wealth is due to luck) and with Musk’s fans ( Musk is very skilled). In fact, the two are not at odds: his skill and determination made him successful and wealthy, but how wealthy he is depends on luck, too. It’s plausible to imagine that in many parallel universes, Musk is also a very successful billionaire, but with how many billions? One , twenty, a hundred? It would still be less than half of his wealth in the current universe. The difference, which makes up for much of his present fortune, must be due to luck.

首先，我要澄清一点，我既同意塔勒布的观点（马斯克的财富很大程度上归功于运气），也同意马斯克粉丝的观点（马斯克确实非常有能力）。事实上，这两者并不矛盾：他的才能和决心成就了他的成功和财富，但他究竟有多富有也取决于运气。我们可以设想，在许多平行宇宙中，马斯克也是一位非常成功的亿万富翁，但他的财富究竟有多少呢？一亿？两亿？还是一亿？即便如此，也还不到他在当前宇宙财富的一半。这其中的差距，也就是他如今财富的很大一部分，必然是运气使然。

Let me repeat – I’m not saying that Musk’s success is due to luck, but that the quantity of his wealth has a major luck component. Just like soccer superstar Cristiano Ronaldo obviously scores thanks to his skill and hard work, but how many goals he will score today significantly depends on luck (and add to this that the variance of wealth is much higher than the variance of goals scored).

让我重申一遍——我并不是说马斯克的成功完全是运气使然，而是说他的财富规模很大程度上受运气影响。就像足球巨星克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多进球固然是靠他的技术和努力，但他今天能进多少球很大程度上取决于运气（而且财富的波动性远高于进球数的波动性）。

This chapter might sound a bit controversial. So , let me clarify what I mean and do not mean.

这一章的内容可能有点争议。所以，让我先解释一下我的意思和不是什么意思。

– Musk’s luck does not take away anything from his talent and determination. A person with the same luck as him but less talent or determination would have achieved far less.

马斯克的运气并不能掩盖他的才华和决心。一个和他运气一样好，但才华或决心不如他的人，成就远不及他。

– Musk’s companies’ extended survival is evidence that he didn’t take extreme risks too often (otherwise, he would have already gone bankrupt). Yet , a few times, he made extreme bets and, therefore, that there is still survivorship bias in the reality we are experiencing.

马斯克旗下公司能够长期存活，证明他并没有经常冒险（否则他早就破产了）。然而，他也曾有过几次孤注一掷的尝试，因此，我们所经历的现实中仍然存在幸存者偏差。

– Some reckless drivers survive a lifetime without crashing, but it doesn’t mean their driving is optimal. It’s optimal only if, given their behavior, the driver didn’t have a significant chance of crashing. Remember : performance is subordinate to survival, and if it seems otherwise, it’s survivorship bias.

有些鲁莽的司机一生都没出过车祸，但这并不意味着他们的驾驶方式就是最优的。只有当考虑到他们的驾驶行为，他们发生车祸的概率很低时，他们的驾驶方式才能称得上最优。记住：驾驶表现要服从于生存，如果看起来并非如此，那就是幸存者偏差。

– Luck being an important factor does not decrease the importance of skill and audaciousness. In fact, it amplifies it. It increases the potential returns of skill and audaciousness.

运气固然重要，但这并不降低技巧和胆识的重要性。事实上，它反而会增强技巧和胆识的重要性，提高技巧和胆识带来的潜在回报。

– The lesson to learn is not that audaciousness is bad. It’s that audaciousness is good, but it must be paired with a good understanding of risk management and of the role of luck.

——我们应该吸取的教训不是说大胆无畏不好，而是说大胆无畏是好事，但必须与对风险管理和运气作用的充分理解相结合。

Similarly , skill is sufficient for becoming rich, but becoming the richest man on Earth also requires a lot of luck. Let me justify this statement with a thought experiment. Imagine taking a thousand entrepreneurs, all with the same starting conditions (cash, connections, etc.) and only differing in skill. Then , let’s observe how their wealth evolves in a few decades. As expected, we would notice that, in general, the more skilled a person is, the wealthier they become. And yet, if you took the wealthiest one amongst them, the chances that they are also the most skilled one are slim. It’s more likely that the richest person is almost as skilled as the most skilled one but considerably luckier.

同样，技能足以致富，但要成为世界首富，运气也必不可少。让我用一个思想实验来佐证这一点。假设有一千位企业家，他们的初始条件（资金、人脉等等）完全相同，唯一的区别在于技能。然后，我们观察他们在几十年内的财富变化。不出所料，我们会发现，一般来说，一个人的技能越高，他就越富有。然而，如果你从中选出最富有的人，他同时也是技能最强的人的概率却很低。更有可能的是，最富有的人技能几乎与技能最强的人不相上下，但运气却好得多。

My point is not about whether Musk deserves his wealth – I couldn’t care less. Instead , my point is about reproducibility. We often wish to imitate the person with the highest score, assuming they are also the most skilled, whereas the most skilled person is more likely to be found among those with a high-but-not-highest score.

我的观点并非在于马斯克是否配得上他的财富——我根本不在乎。相反，我的观点在于可复制性。我们常常想要模仿得分最高的人，并想当然地认为他们也是最有技能的，但实际上，最有技能的人更有可能出现在那些得分很高但并非最高的人当中。

Note that I wrote “more likely.” There may be someone so skilled that he ends up with the highest score. But he must be that much more skilled than everyone else. Otherwise , the chances are that one of the many “great-but-not-best” participants will get enough luckier than the best one to overcome the difference in skill.

请注意我用的是“更有可能”。或许有人技艺超群，最终获得最高分。但他必须比其他所有人都强得多。否则，众多“优秀但并非最佳”的参赛者中，很可能有人运气比最佳选手好得多，从而弥补技艺上的差距。

That said, my point is not “don’t imitate the best one” or “imitate the second-best one.” Instead , it’s “be critical about whose strategies you aim to imitate and why.”

也就是说，我的观点并不是“不要模仿最好的”或者“要模仿次好的”，而是“要批判性地思考你想要模仿谁的策略以及为什么要模仿”。

Ask yourself, how reproducible is that strategy? In ten parallel universes, in how many do they end up as successful as in this one, and in how many do they end up bankrupt or in jail? Are you okay with not only the outcome in the current universe but also with the full range of outcomes across universes?

扪心自问，这种策略的可复制性如何？在十个平行宇宙中，有多少个宇宙里的他们最终会像这个宇宙一样成功？又有多少个宇宙里的他们最终会破产或锒铛入狱？你是否能够接受的不仅是当前宇宙的结果，还有所有宇宙中可能出现的各种结果？

Moreover , consider another point Taleb made. “ You get to the tail by increasing the variance (or the scale) rather than raising the expectation.” In other words, to get extreme outcomes, you must often reduce average outcomes. Do you really want to be the one with the highest score? It will probably come at a cost. Not just effort and opportunity costs but also risk – risk that will increase the best outcome but decrease the average outcome.

此外，还要考虑塔勒布提出的另一点：“要想达到极端结果，增加方差（或规模）比提高预期更重要。”换句话说，为了获得极端结果，你往往必须降低平均结果。你真的想成为得分最高的人吗？这很可能要付出代价。不仅是努力和机会成本，还有风险——这种风险会提高最佳结果，但会降低平均结果。

Let me explain this last point with another thought experiment. Again , let’s take a thousand entrepreneurs, all with the same starting conditions (money, connections, etc.) and only differing in skill. Five hundred of them take extreme risks, whereas the rest only take small risks. Let’s observe what would happen after a few years in ten parallel universes. We would notice that, in all universes, the wealthiest entrepreneur would come from the risk-taking group. However , and this is the key point, in each of the ten universes, it would be a different person! Each of these ten people would have extreme success when lucky and terrible outcomes when unlucky. In contrast, a skilled person who only takes moderate risks would have great-though-not-extreme outcomes in almost all parallel universes.

让我用另一个思想实验来解释最后一点。假设有一千名创业者，他们的初始条件（资金、人脉等等）完全相同，唯一的区别在于技能水平。其中五百人承担极高的风险，而其余五百人则只承担较小的风险。让我们观察几年后在十个平行宇宙中会发生什么。我们会发现，在所有宇宙中，最富有的创业者都来自承担风险的那组人。然而，关键在于，在每个宇宙中，最富有的创业者都不同！这十个人在运气好的时候会取得巨大的成功，在运气不好的时候则会遭遇惨痛的失败。相比之下，一个技能娴熟、只承担适度风险的人，在几乎所有平行宇宙中都能取得可观但并非极致的成功。

If you don’t take extreme risks, even if you’re the most skilled person, you will be outperformed by someone who does. And if you take extreme risks, you will have worse average outcomes than if you didn’t.

如果你不承担极端风险，即使你是最有能力的人，也会被那些敢于冒险的人超越。而如果你承担极端风险，你的平均结果反而会比不冒险更差。

Let me clarify a few things. First , this doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t take risks – here, we’re talking about extreme risks, bets that damage you irreparably when they go wrong. In general, taking small risks is a good strategy. Remember the content of an earlier chapter: “ Distinguish between calculated risks whose consequences you can recover from and recklessness whose consequences might permanently debilitate you. There is a sweet spot where you expose yourself to the former but not the latter – that’s a good place to aim.”

让我澄清几点。首先，这并不意味着你不应该承担风险——这里我们指的是极端风险，一旦失败就会给你造成无法挽回的损失。一般来说，承担小风险是一种不错的策略。请记住前面章节的内容：“区分经过计算的风险（其后果可以弥补）和鲁莽的风险（其后果可能永久性地损害你的身心健康）。存在一个最佳平衡点，让你既承担前者的风险，又避免后者的风险——这才是应该努力的方向。”

Second , this doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t set ambitious goals for yourself. It means that, while choosing your strategy to achieve them, you should be wary of survivorship bias and refuse strategies that merely improve your maximum potential outcome without also improving your distribution of outcomes. More on this in my 2024 book, “ Winning Long - Term Games .”

其次，这并不意味着你不应该为自己设定远大的目标。而是说，在选择实现目标的策略时，你应该警惕幸存者偏差，并拒绝那些仅仅提高最大潜在结果而没有改善结果分布的策略。更多内容请参见我2024年出版的《赢得长期博弈》一书。

Third , it means that you shouldn’t feel bad if someone who took excessive risks and has a worse distribution of outcomes than yours got more successful than you. Remember that you and they played different games, with different goals and thus different optimal strategies. Their victory doesn’t invalidate your choice.

第三，这意味着如果有人承担了过高的风险，并且结果分布比你更差，却最终比你更成功，你也不应该感到沮丧。记住，你和他们玩的是不同的游戏，有着不同的目标，因此也采取了不同的最优策略。他们的胜利并不能否定你的选择。

1 Source: https://twitter.com/nntaleb/status/1534172773580513280.

1 来源：https://twitter.com/nntaleb/status/1534172773580513280。

THE HIDDEN SIDE OF NON-ERGODICITY

非遍历性的隐秘一面

Non -ergodicity is often seen as something undesirable, but there are cases in which it is desirable.

非遍历性通常被认为是不好的，但在某些情况下，它是可取的。

Take the example of baking. Ten inexperienced people baking a cake are likely to produce ten bad cakes. Conversely , an inexperienced person baking ten cakes is likely to produce two bad cakes and eight good ones, as she learns and improves. Because the population outcome (ten bad cakes) is different from the lifetime outcome (two bad cakes and eight good ones), baking cakes is non-ergodic. But it’s good! The source of irreversibility here is learning, and that’s something desirable. 1

以烘焙为例。十个没有经验的人一起烤蛋糕，很可能做出十个难吃的蛋糕。相反，一个没有经验的人烤十个蛋糕，很可能做出两个难吃的蛋糕和八个好吃的蛋糕，因为她会不断学习和改进。由于总体结果（十个难吃的蛋糕）与个体最终结果（两个难吃的蛋糕和八个好吃的蛋糕）不同，所以烘焙蛋糕是非遍历的。但这很好！这种不可逆性的根源在于学习，而学习是可取的。

Non -ergodicity is undesirable when the lifetime outcome is lower than the population one but desirable when it’s higher.

当终生结果低于总体结果时，非遍历性是不理想的；但当终生结果高于总体结果时，非遍历性是理想的。

# ↩

Examples of positive non-ergodicity

正非遍历性的例子

Learning . If you ensure that past errors won’t happen again (i.e., you introduced positive irreversibility), good for you!

学习。如果你能确保过去的错误不会再次发生（即，你引入了积极的不可逆性），那就太好了！

Relationships . Going on a date with the same person ten times produces different outcomes than going on ten dates with ten people. 2

人际关系。和同一个人约会十次与和十个人约会十次的结果截然不同。

Customer acquisition. In some businesses, showing your product once to a thousand customers will convert a few of them into clients, but showing it ten times to a hundred customers will convert more.

客户获取。在某些行业，向一千名潜在客户展示一次产品，可能只会转化出少数客户；但向一百名潜在客户展示十次，转化率就会更高。

Skin in the game. As we saw in Chapter 5, in some domains, society relies on irreversible damage at the individual level. For example, the fact that bad drivers die in car incidents or lose their driving licenses keeps other drivers safe. In this case, negative non-ergodicity at the individual level translates into positive ergodicity at the collective level.

利益攸关。正如我们在第五章中所看到的，在某些领域，社会依赖于个体层面的不可逆转的损害。例如，不良驾驶员在交通事故中丧生或被吊销驾照，这保障了其他驾驶员的安全。在这种情况下，个体层面的负向非遍历性转化为集体层面的正向遍历性。

# ↩

Looking for positive non-ergodicity

寻找正的非遍历性

Ergodicity is not an ideal to achieve; when non-ergodicity is positive, you might want to cultivate it to some degree. The best approach is not to focus on labels but to use the techniques described in this book to analyze situations in their practical outcomes over appropriate time horizons.

遍历性并非理想状态；当非遍历性具有积极作用时，不妨在一定程度上加以培养。最佳方法并非着眼于标签，而是运用本书所述的技巧，在适当的时间范围内分析各种情况的实际结果。

1 Much of manufacturing management, and management in general, is about ensuring that no incident will happen again for the same reason. In this case, irreversibility is sought after.

1. 制造管理以及一般意义上的管理，其核心在于确保不会因同样的原因再次发生事故。在这种情况下，人们追求的是不可逆性。

2 That doesn’t mean that an initial phase of expanding your options (with many dates) isn’t a good idea; as with many things in life, the best approach is an alternation of expansion and compression – which, incidentally, is the same base algorithm used by the cortex (more on this: my 2019 paper “Techniques for the Emergence of Meaning in Machine Learning.”)

2 这并不意味着在初期阶段扩大选择范围（多约会）不是一个好主意；就像生活中的许多事情一样，最好的方法是扩张和压缩交替进行——顺便说一句，这正是大脑皮层使用的基本算法（更多内容请参见我的 2019 年论文《机器学习中意义涌现的技术》）。

第九部分
# ↩

OTHER EXAMPLES OF NON-ERGODICITY

非遍历性的其他例子

This last part of the book presents a few more examples of non-ergodicity.

本书最后一部分给出了一些非遍历性的例子。

BEHAVIORAL CHANGE

行为改变

I f you manage to brush your teeth after dinner for thirty days straight, you’re likely to have formed a lifetime habit. Conversely , if you brush them only once a week, you might go for your whole life without having formed a habit of brushing your teeth.

如果你能连续三十天在晚餐后刷牙，你很可能就会养成终身习惯。相反，如果你每周只刷一次牙，你可能一辈子都无法养成刷牙的习惯。

Not only do habits take repetition, but they also take consistency. It is not just about how many times you perform a habit. Instead , it’s about how many times you perform it within a short period.

习惯的养成不仅需要重复，更需要持之以恒。关键不在于你做了多少次习惯，而在于你在短时间内做了多少次。

Behavioral change is non-ergodic. The distribution of efforts matters.

行为改变并非遍历过程。努力的分配至关重要。

# ↩

The importance of achieving critical mass

达到临界质量的重要性

I spend part of my time helping organizations build a culture of operational excellence. I have observed with my eyes hundreds of companies. I do not know of a single one that built desired habits without obsessing over it for a short period. If a manager can keep their team focused on getting one thing right all the time for about 2-4 weeks, they will have created a lasting habit.

我花一些时间帮助企业建立卓越运营文化。我亲眼观察过数百家公司，没有一家公司能在不经过短期专注的情况下养成理想的习惯。如果一位管理者能让团队在两到四周内始终专注于做好一件事，他们就能培养出一种持久的习惯。

Conversely , I have seen many companies whose managers remind their workers about the desired behavior once a week for years. They obtain no results. Of course – they fail to achieve the critical mass required in the minds of their team members to build a habit.

相反，我见过很多公司的管理者每周都提醒员工应该如何表现，而且持续好几年。结果却毫无成效。当然，他们没能在团队成员心中形成足够的共识，从而无法养成习惯。

Managers who ignore the non-ergodic nature of behavioral change waste their time and achieve no result. Conversely , those who acknowledge it get quick successes that compound over time.

忽视行为改变非遍历性的管理者会浪费时间，一事无成。相反，那些认识到这一点的管理者能够迅速取得成功，并且随着时间的推移，这种成功会不断累积。

38
# ↩

NARROWNESS, BROADNESS, AND ERGODICITY

狭窄性、宽广性和遍历性

A t the beginning of this book, we saw that what is optimal for winning a single race is not optimal for winning a championship. Of course, both require skills and athleticism. But on top of that, a championship also requires some sustainability. You shouldn’t give it all and risk your life or your joints, not as much as you could if all that mattered was a single race.

本书开篇我们就提到，赢得单场比赛的最佳策略并非赢得总冠军的最佳策略。当然，两者都需要技巧和运动能力。但除此之外，赢得总冠军还需要一定的持久性。你不应该像赢得单场比赛那样拼尽全力，甚至危及生命或关节健康。

The same can be said within a race. If you are a top skier, it is relatively easy to be the fastest in a single slope. Just go down without caring about the next turn, your knees, or your life.

同样的道理也适用于比赛。如果你是一名顶尖滑雪运动员，那么在单条雪道上成为最快选手相对容易。只需一路滑下去，无需顾虑下一个弯道、膝盖或生命安全。

The easiest way to increase performance is to narrow the time frame over which it is measured.

提高绩效的最简单方法是缩短衡量绩效的时间范围。

Sadly , it is also the easiest way to produce unsustainable performance.

遗憾的是，这也是造成不可持续绩效的最简单方法。

If your tactic to go faster is to do as if there were no negative consequences, you will go faster, and then you will suffer from the negative consequences. It’s probably not a trade-off worth making.

如果你为了追求速度而采取不计后果的策略，你的确会加速，但最终也会承受负面后果。这恐怕不是值得的权衡。

# ↩

Sustainable performance

可持续绩效

If you want to ski fast, it’s very easy. Just keep your skis straight, your knees bent, and go down the slope as straight as possible. You will have a hard time avoiding a crash, but for a few seconds, you will be fast.

想滑得快其实很简单。只需保持雪板笔直，膝盖弯曲，尽可能笔直地滑下坡。虽然很难避免摔倒，但几秒钟内你的速度会非常快。

Most people can be fast. The hard part is being fast while retaining control, to be fast in the short term and the long term.

大多数人速度都很快。难点在于如何在保持速度的同时保持控制力，既要保证短期内的速度，也要保证长期内的速度。

The easiest way to increase short-term performance is to do so at the cost of long-term performance. It is hardly a tradeoff you want to make. My cousin did it, and his career ultimately suffered from it.

提升短期业绩最简单的方法就是以牺牲长期业绩为代价。这绝对不是你想做的权衡。我表弟就这么做了，结果他的事业最终因此受损。

Here are some other examples of the same tradeoff.

以下是一些体现这种权衡取舍的其他例子。

– Any salesperson can easily post record sales this month. The hard part is to do it without using discounts or deception, so that neither the brand nor the profits suffer.

任何销售人员本月都可以轻松创下销售纪录。难点在于如何在不使用折扣或欺骗手段的情况下做到这一点，从而既不损害品牌形象，也不损害利润。

– Many people can have a great career at something. The hard part is to do it while keeping a healthy personal life.

很多人都能在某个领域取得辉煌的成就。难点在于如何在事业成功的同时保持健康的个人生活。

– Any restaurant manager can make the business more efficient by buying cheaper ingredients. The hard part is to cut costs while keeping quality high.

任何餐厅经理都可以通过购买更便宜的食材来提高经营效率。难点在于如何在降低成本的同时保持高品质。

# ↩

Restricting the scope

限制范围

We can generalize the previous examples as follows.

我们可以将前面的例子概括如下。

The easiest way to increase performance is to restrict the scope of its definition. For example, we can restrict the definition of fast from “fast during a whole championship” to “fast in this particular slope,” or restrict the definition of happiness from “a fulfilling career, a happy family, a good social life, and a healthy body” to “a prestigious job title” or “a coveted spouse.”

提高绩效最简单的方法就是缩小其定义范围。例如，我们可以将“快”的定义从“整个锦标赛期间的速度快”缩小到“在这个特定坡道上的速度快”，或者将“幸福”的定义从“一份令人满意的事业、一个幸福的家庭、良好的社交生活和健康的身体”缩小到“一份令人艳羡的职位”或“一个令人向往的伴侣”。

In both cases, we make the outcome easier to achieve, but it will also matter less and for a shorter time.

无论哪种情况，我们都能让结果更容易实现，但结果的重要性也会降低，持续时间也会缩短。

Moreover , we open the door to undesired consequences. Maximizing our speed not across the whole championship or even across the race but on one particular slope might lead to us going too fast and crashing shortly afterward. Optimizing our relationship choices, or even our life, to achieve a marriage with a spouse envied by our friends might lead to a quick divorce.

此外，这样做会招致不必要的后果。如果我们不是在整个锦标赛甚至整场比赛中追求速度最大化，而是在某个特定的坡道上追求速度最大化，可能会导致速度过快，随后发生碰撞。同样，如果我们为了拥有一个令朋友羡慕的伴侣而优化我们的人际关系选择，甚至优化我们的人生，则可能导致迅速离婚。

# ↩

Expanding the scope

扩大范围

On the other hand, the easiest way to hide problems is to increase the scope of measurement.

另一方面，掩盖问题的最简单方法就是扩大测量范围。

If a town has a few districts whose population lives in poverty, it can conveniently hide the problem by talking about the average income measured across the city as a whole.

如果一个城镇有几个地区的居民生活在贫困之中，那么它可以通过谈论整个城市的平均收入来巧妙地掩盖这个问题。

If your romantic life is in shambles, you can conveniently hide the problem by measuring your happiness across all your activities, including your career and your friends.

如果你的爱情生活一团糟，你可以通过将幸福感衡量为你所有活动的幸福感，包括你的事业和朋友关系，来巧妙地掩盖这个问题。

We saw how reducing the scope of measurement to increase performance opens the door to undesired consequences. Expanding the scope of measurement to hide problems leads to them too. Problems grow the size they need for them to be acknowledged. A hidden problem is a problem that keeps growing, hurting us more painfully in the future. For example, social unrest is not a problem for the wealthier part of the population until riots start and ignored health problems grow to threaten our lives.

我们已经看到，为了提升绩效而缩小衡量范围，会引发诸多不良后果。同样，为了掩盖问题而扩大衡量范围，也会导致问题出现。问题会不断扩大，直到被人们注意到。被掩盖的问题会持续恶化，在未来给我们带来更严重的伤害。例如，社会动荡对于富裕阶层来说可能并非问题，直到骚乱爆发，被忽视的健康问题恶化到威胁生命为止。

# ↩

Ergodicity and scope

遍历性和范围

Ergodicity provides us with a few tools to recognize whether, in a given context, it is safe to expand or restrict the scope of measurement. In general, in non-ergodic contexts, it is not safe to do so.

遍历性为我们提供了几种工具，用于判断在特定情况下扩大或缩小测量范围是否安全。一般来说，在非遍历性情况下，这样做是不安全的。

Whether a context is ergodic can tell us:

上下文是否具有遍历性可以告诉我们：

– If it is safe to optimize short-term performance, or whether we should care about securing sustainability first. Had my cousin known about ergodicity, he would have known that skiing each race as if it were the last one might actually make it become the last one.

——优化短期绩效是否安全，还是我们应该首先关注可持续性？如果我表弟了解遍历性，他就会明白，把每一场比赛都当作最后一场比赛来对待，可能真的会让它变成最后一场比赛。

– If it is safe to use averages, or whether we should consider more granular data. Had we known that, we would have managed the pandemic better (as described in the previous chapter).

——使用平均值是否安全，或者我们是否应该考虑更细致的数据。如果我们早知道这一点，我们就能更好地应对疫情（如前一章所述）。

– Why so many employees burn out. A company cares about performance across all its employees in a given month, but an employee cares about their own performance across their whole career. Different scopes create a conflict of interest between employees and their employer, even if both care about the same metric, performance.

——为什么这么多员工会精疲力竭？公司关注的是所有员工在特定月份的整体绩效，而员工关注的是自己整个职业生涯的绩效。即使双方都关注同一个指标——绩效，不同的关注点也会造成员工和雇主之间的利益冲突。

# ↩

Efficiency and effectiveness

效率和效能

The tension described above between short-term and long-term performance is similar to the difference between efficiency and effectiveness. When a skier goes down the hill at full speed, he is efficient. He only needs a few seconds to complete the slope. When a skier has a long career full of medals, he is effective.

上文所述的短期表现与长期表现之间的矛盾，类似于效率与效能之间的区别。当滑雪运动员全速滑下山坡时，他展现的是效率，因为他只需几秒钟就能完成滑行。而当滑雪运动员拥有漫长的职业生涯并斩获众多奖牌时，他展现的是效能。

The difference between efficiency and effectiveness is that the former is a snapshot in time, and the latter describes a lifetime. Or , to be more precise, efficiency is restricted by time (in that case, the duration of the race), whereas effectiveness is expanded across time, encompassing an entire lifetime. What is efficient in the short term might or might not be effective in the long term.

效率和效能的区别在于，前者反映的是某一时刻的状态，而后者则描述的是一生的状态。更准确地说，效率受时间限制（在这种情况下，指的是比赛的持续时间），而效能则跨越时间，涵盖整个人生。短期内有效的方法，长期来看未必有效。

# ↩

Summary of this chapter

本章概要

– The easiest way to increase performance is to restrict the scope of its definition. Sadly , it is also the easiest way to incur problems.

提高性能最简单的方法是缩小其定义范围。遗憾的是，这也是最容易引发问题的方法。

– The easiest way to hide problems is to expand the scope of measurement.

掩盖问题的最简单方法就是扩大测量范围。

– Ergodicity determines whether it is safe to restrict or expand the scope of measurement.

遍历性决定了限制或扩大测量范围是否安全。

SUSTAINING PERFORMANCE

保持绩效

A s I write these lines, legendary investor Warren Buffett is the seventh richest person on Earth . He made 99.7% of his fortune after his 52nd birthday and 30% after his 83 rd birthday. 1

在我写下这些文字的时候，传奇投资人沃伦·巴菲特是全球第七大富豪。他99.7%的财富是在52岁之后积累的，30%是在83岁之后积累的。

Of course, his skills in producing high returns mattered. 2 But his skills in avoiding bankruptcy mattered more. 3 If he had gone bankrupt before the age of 60, as many “brilliant” investors did, he would have been forgotten.

当然，他创造高回报的能力固然重要。但更重要的是他避免破产的能力。如果他像许多“杰出”的投资者那样，在60岁之前破产，他就会被人遗忘。

As Morgan Housel wrote, “ If your investment returns are in the 50th percentile every year, you will probably end up in the top 5-10% over a 20-year period.” That’s because most aren’t able to sustain performance.

正如摩根·豪塞尔所写，“如果你的投资回报率每年都处于前50%，那么20年后你很可能会跻身前5-10%。”这是因为大多数人无法保持这样的业绩。

# ↩

Unsustainable performance

不可持续的表现

Energy company Enron was awarded Fortune magazine’s “ America’s most innovative company” award for six years between 1996 and 2001. It then filed for bankruptcy in the same year, 2001.

能源公司安然在 1996 年至 2001 年期间连续六年获得《财富》杂志“美国最具创新力公司”奖。同年，即 2001 年，该公司申请破产。

The problem with these awards is that they look at returns without also considering sustainability. They look at who makes the most smoke without checking whether they’re burning their house in the process. 4

这些奖项的问题在于，它们只关注收益，却忽略了可持续性。它们只看谁制造的烟雾最多，却不去考察他们是否在过程中烧毁了自己的房子。

It is easy to make money. I could sell my kidney or scam someone. It is much harder to do so in a way that doesn’t compromise my life.

赚钱很容易。我可以卖肾，也可以骗人。但要以一种不损害我生命的方式赚钱，就难多了。

In real life, consequences matter and are there to stay. Sustainability is often a larger obstacle to performance than talent. Few are willing to sacrifice their marriage, their health, their reputation, or anything else that, if lost, is hard or impossible to get back. As a result, they make conservative choices.

在现实生活中，后果至关重要，而且无法抹去。可持续性往往比天赋更能阻碍绩效的提升。很少有人愿意牺牲婚姻、健康、名誉或其他任何一旦失去就难以或无法挽回的东西。因此，他们会做出保守的选择。

Are they really sacrificing returns by making these conservative choices, though? Or are they maximizing them?

他们采取这些保守策略真的会牺牲收益吗？还是说他们正在最大化收益？

# ↩

Leading and lagging indicators

领先指标和滞后指标

Readers of my two books on management, “ Best Practices for Operational Excellence ” and “ Teams Are Adaptive Systems ,” are familiar with my thoughts around indicators. All companies track indicators such as revenue, profit, and incidents. These are called lagging indicators, for they describe what has already happened.

读过我的两本管理学著作——《卓越运营最佳实践》和《团队是适应性系统》的读者，应该对我的指标理论有所了解。所有公司都会追踪诸如收入、利润和事故等指标。这些被称为滞后指标，因为它们描述的是已经发生的事情。

Some companies also track leading indicators. These measure factors influencing the future performance of the company. For example, the behaviors expressed by the employees, their skills, the hours of training done, the number of clients visiting or visited, and so on.

一些公司还会追踪领先指标。这些指标衡量影响公司未来业绩的因素。例如，员工的行为、技能、培训时长、到访或已到访的客户数量等等。

There are many benefits to tracking leading indicators in addition to lagging ones. For example, suppose that you measure how many employees of your company wear personal protective equipment (a leading indicator). If you discover that many do not wear them, you have a chance to correct the situation before one of them gets injured. Conversely , if you estimate the safety of your workplace by only measuring incidents (a lagging indicator), you will only take action after the damage is done.

除了滞后指标之外，追踪领先指标还有许多好处。例如，假设您统计公司有多少员工佩戴个人防护装备（领先指标）。如果您发现很多员工没有佩戴，您就有机会在有人受伤之前纠正这种情况。相反，如果您仅仅通过统计事故数量（滞后指标）来评估工作场所的安全状况，那么您只能在损失发生后才采取行动。

Measuring leading indicators allows you to spot problems before they get a chance to cause irreparable damage. Instead , relying on lagging indicators ensures that you will eventually get hit by irreversibility.

衡量领先指标能让你在问题造成不可挽回的损失之前发现它们。相反，依赖滞后指标最终只会让你遭受不可逆转的打击。

# ↩

Achieving sustained performance

实现持续绩效

Most frustration comes from doing the necessary believing it is sufficient. Hence , let me clarify that the contents of this paragraph are not sufficient to achieve sustained performance but merely necessary.

大多数挫败感源于误以为做了必要的事情就足够了。因此，我想澄清一下，本段内容并非实现持续绩效的充分条件，而仅仅是必要条件。

I believe that to achieve sustained performance, it is necessary to measure leading indicators. They will keep you on track, allowing you to outlast your competitors, even if they are more skilled or wealthier. They will give you chances to avoid game-overs. They will show you where what others call luck resides.

我认为，要实现持续的卓越表现，必须衡量领先指标。它们能让你保持正确的方向，即使竞争对手更有能力或更有财力，也能让你坚持到最后。它们能让你有机会避免失败。它们能让你看到别人所谓的“运气”究竟在哪里。

Conversely , relying on lagging indicators is not enough. They mislead the observer to go all-in during an ephemeral success, causing him to be destroyed by the following regression to the mean. They introduce a false sense of security by not measuring problems until they’re big enough to cause irreparable damage or by not spotting success until it is apparent (and therefore dissuading everyone but the most determined).

反之，仅仅依赖滞后指标是不够的。它们会误导观察者在短暂的成功中孤注一掷，导致随后的均值回归使其遭受重创。它们会给人一种虚假的安全感，因为只有在问题严重到足以造成不可挽回的损失时才会发现问题，或者只有在成功显而易见时才会注意到成功（因此，除了最坚定的人之外，几乎所有人都望而却步）。

By giving you a chance to react to problems before they hurt you irreparably, leading indicators increase your ergodicity. Conversely , relying on lagging ones decreases it.

领先指标让你有机会在问题造成不可挽回的损失之前做出反应，从而提高你的遍历能力。相反，依赖滞后指标会降低你的遍历能力。

Choose wisely what to measure.

谨慎选择测量对象。

1 At the moment of writing his book, Buffett is 90 years old. The first piece of data on him is dated 2018, and the second, 2020.

1. 巴菲特撰写本书时已90岁高龄。关于他的第一条数据日期为2018年，第二条数据日期为2020年。

2 And so did his skills at being active in a secular bull market.

2 他在长期牛市中积极参与的技能也同样如此。

3 Much of the returns of investing come from compounding – the fact that the returns of an investment produce returns of their own. For example, $100 invested in a venture that returns 10% a year yields $10 a year. However, if the returns are invested back in, the second year the yield will be $11, then $12.1, $15.8 after 30 years, and $106.7 after 50 years. It escalates quickly.

3. 投资的大部分回报都来自复利——即投资回报本身就能产生回报。例如，投资100美元到一个年回报率为10%的项目，每年可获得10美元的收益。但是，如果将收益再投资，第二年收益将达到11美元，然后是12.1美元，30年后达到15.8美元，50年后达到106.7美元。收益增长速度非常快。

Being able to stay in the game for a long time pays a lot.

能够长期留在赛场上是有回报的。

4 A naïve metaphor would be that of “regression to the mean.” While often correct, it misses the point that a company could be wildly successful and continue to be successful. One cannot dismiss an exceptional result as noise; one must prove that the underlying distribution of future outcomes for the company at hand is still a mediocre one.

4. 一个简单的比喻是“均值回归”。虽然这种比喻通常是正确的，但它忽略了一个关键点：一家公司可能取得巨大成功，并且能够持续成功。我们不能将一个非凡的业绩视为噪音；我们必须证明，该公司未来业绩的潜在分布仍然是平庸的。

A better remark would be that these awards are only based on lagging indicators – metrics that measure the past. Instead, a serious award would complement lagging indicators with leading ones – metrics that measure the fundaments of success.

更准确的说法是，这些奖项仅仅基于滞后指标——衡量过去的指标。而真正有价值的奖项应该将滞后指标与领先指标相结合——领先指标衡量成功的根本所在。

# ↩

THE TRAGEDY OF THE COMMONS

公地悲剧

T he classic example of the tragedy of the commons is as follows. There is a village near a small pond (the “common”). Self -interest would dictate its citizens to catch as much fish as possible. But if everyone does that, the fish population disappears (the “tragedy”).

公地悲剧的经典例子如下。村子附近有一个小池塘（“公地”）。出于自身利益，村民们会尽可能多地捕鱼。但如果每个人都这样做，鱼类就会消失（“悲剧”）。

In a reply to a post of mine, 1 Rory Sutherland connected the idea of ergodicity to actions that are rational if one person does it but disastrous when everyone does it. This made me wonder if the tragedy of the commons could be formulated in terms of ergodicity – and it can.

在回复我的一篇帖子时， 1 Rory Sutherland 将遍历性的概念与这样一种行为联系起来：如果只有一个人做，那就是理性的；但如果每个人都做，那就是灾难性的。这让我思考，公地悲剧是否可以用遍历性来解释——答案是肯定的。

We have seen how ergodicity is satisfied only when the lifetime and population outcomes coincide. What about the pond example above? If a single villager catches a fish a day, he can sustain himself indefinitely, but if the whole village goes fishing the same day, they can have a luncheon but will starve over the following weeks. The two outcomes are different; therefore, tragedies of the commons are non-ergodic.

我们已经看到，只有当生命周期结果和人口数量结果一致时，遍历性才能得到满足。那么，上面提到的池塘例子呢？如果一个村民每天捕到一条鱼，他就能无限期地维持生存；但如果全村人都在同一天去捕鱼，他们虽然可以吃顿午饭，但接下来的几周就会挨饿。这两种结果截然不同；因此，公地悲剧是非遍历性的。

# ↩

Fatigue

疲劳

Imagine that the pond is very large and contains thousands of fish. How many fish can each villager capture a day without endangering the fish population?

假设池塘非常大，里面有成千上万条鱼。每个村民每天最多可以捕捞多少条鱼，才能不危及鱼类种群数量？

The answer depends on the fish’s reproduction rate. In general, the villagers can only fish as many fishes as the number of newborns. 2 If the villagers fish more than that, the fish population shrinks over time; and if they fish less than that, the fish population grows.

答案取决于鱼的繁殖率。一般来说，村民捕捞的鱼的数量只能与新生鱼的数量相当。如果村民捕捞的鱼超过这个数量，鱼群数量就会随着时间推移而减少；如果捕捞的鱼少于这个数量，鱼群数量就会增长。

The technical name of this phenomenon is fatigue. It is found in many contexts of life. For example, some sports cause mini-injuries to our muscles and ligaments. If we practice them too frequently, ligaments are damaged faster than our body can repair them, and after some time, we might find ourselves with a torn ligament. Again , what matters is the ratio between damage speed and recovery speed.

这种现象的专业名称是疲劳。它存在于生活的方方面面。例如，某些运动会对我们的肌肉和韧带造成轻微损伤。如果我们练习过于频繁，韧带受损的速度就会超过身体的修复速度，一段时间后，我们可能会发现韧带撕裂。关键在于损伤速度和恢复速度之间的比例。

In general, whenever damage speed is faster than recovery speed, fatigue occurs. If this continues for long enough, fatigue failure occurs. 3

一般来说，当损伤速度快于恢复速度时，就会发生疲劳。如果这种情况持续足够长的时间，就会发生疲劳失效。

Fatigue is the characteristic phenomenon of tragedies of the common.

疲劳是普通人悲剧的典型特征。

# ↩

Fatigue and ergodicity

疲劳和遍历性

Fatigue is a strange beast. Up to a point, it is reversible. If you over-exert yourself and notice before any injury, a bit of rest can lead to full recovery. However , beyond a certain point, fatigue is irreversible. Some injuries cannot be fully recovered from. And to make things more complex, regular exercise alternated to enough rest can make you stronger, thus able to withstand higher loads without hurting yourself.

疲劳是一种很奇特的现象。在某种程度上，它是可逆的。如果你过度劳累，并且在受伤之前就注意到，稍作休息就能完全恢复。然而，超过某个临界点，疲劳就不可逆转了。有些伤病甚至无法完全康复。更复杂的是，规律的锻炼与充足的休息交替进行，可以增强体质，从而能够承受更大的负荷而不受伤。

This pattern is the reason I chose fatigue as the last chapter. Over the book, we’ve examined scenarios as if the actor, the activity, and the exposure of the former to the latter were fixed in time – determined at the beginning of the analysis and then assumed constant. However , in real life, not only can these properties change over time, but they often change based on what happened to them at the previous time steps. For example, an athlete who suffers a minor injury from excessive training might learn his lesson and train more properly, reducing the chances of future larger injuries.

正是基于这种模式，我才选择疲劳作为最后一章。在本书中，我们一直假设行动者、活动以及行动者与活动之间的接触程度在时间上是固定不变的——在分析之初就已确定，并假定为常数。然而，在现实生活中，这些属性不仅会随时间变化，而且往往会根据之前时间步长发生的情况而改变。例如，一名运动员如果因过度训练而受轻伤，可能会吸取教训，更加合理地进行训练，从而降低未来发生更严重伤病的风险。

How these properties influence each other is a subject too complex and too domain-specific to be discussed here. However , I will leave you with a final comment. Applying the three strategies discussed so far (limiting exposure, skin in the game, and redistribution) is more important than knowing how the system works. Relying on knowledge makes one prone to complacency, over-optimization, and the Ludic Fallacy . 4

这些属性如何相互影响是一个过于复杂且领域特定的主题，无法在此详述。不过，我最后想补充一点：应用目前讨论过的三种策略（限制风险、利益攸关和利益再分配）比了解系统如何运作更为重要。依赖知识会使人容易陷入自满、过度优化和游戏谬误。

Conversely , limiting exposure, skin in the game, and redistribution not only makes you less likely to suffer from events you couldn’t predict but also enables learning and, thus, self-correction.

反之，限制风险暴露、风险承担和风险再分配，不仅能降低你遭受无法预测的事件影响的可能性，还能让你学习，从而进行自我纠正。

Without limiting exposure, one cannot learn from mistakes, for mistakes can spell “permanent game-over.” If you go all in and lose, you don’t have a second chance to apply what you have learned.

如果不限制接触范围，就无法从错误中吸取教训，因为错误可能意味着“彻底失败”。如果你孤注一掷却失败了，你就没有第二次机会运用所学到的知识。

Without skin in the game, one might learn the wrong lessons or learn from the wrong people. Skin in the game is the dampener of recklessness; without it, recklessness begets more recklessness.

如果没有切身利益，人们可能会学到错误的经验，或者从错误的人那里学习。切身利益能够抑制鲁莽行为；没有切身利益，鲁莽行为只会滋生更多的鲁莽行为。

And without redistribution, even small events can have irreversible consequences. Without a system to redistribute patients between hospitals, even a local outbreak might result in an overwhelmed hospital.

如果没有重新分配机制，即使是小规模的疫情也可能造成不可逆转的后果。如果没有医院间病人重新分配系统，即使是局部疫情爆发也可能导致医院不堪重负。

Hence , the importance of understanding ergodicity and its practical applications: it makes less important to understand everything else.

因此，理解遍历性及其实际应用的重要性就体现出来了：理解其他一切事物的重要性就降低了。

1 https://twitter.com/rorysutherland/status/1367555119479480323

1 https://twitter.com/rorysutherland/status/1367555119479480323

2 A more complete answer would consider the fact that fishes might die of natural causes before they get to reproduce. Therefore, it would be: “the number of fishes born each day that are expected to reproduce.”

2. 更完整的答案应该考虑到鱼类可能在繁殖前因自然原因死亡。因此，答案应该是：“每天出生的鱼中预计能够繁殖的鱼的数量”。

In brittleness, it is the ratio between the speed of damage propagation and the speed of load propagation. For the readers interested in the mechanical aspects of fatigue and brittleness, I recommend the first three sections of my paper “The Dynamics of Risk-Taking.”

4 Believing that the system must conform to accepted rules.

4. 认为系统必须符合公认的规则。

# ↩

CONCLUSIONS

结论

I n the first half of this book, I explained how mistaking a non-ergodic system for an ergodic one causes wrong decisions. In particular:

本书前半部分解释了将非遍历系统误认为遍历系统会导致错误决策的原因。具体来说：

– In the first part of the book, I showed how irreversibility causes losses to absorb future gains.

– 在本书的第一部分，我阐述了不可逆性如何导致损失吸收未来的收益。

– In the second part, we saw how systems can work on average and still fail locally, if losses are irreversible for their local components.

– 在第二部分中，我们看到，如果局部组件的损失是不可逆的，那么系统平均而言可以正常工作，但局部仍然会发生故障。

– In the third part, we learned that a system is non-ergodic if the lifetime outcomes of its participants do not coincide with the expected outcome.

– 在第三部分中，我们了解到，如果一个系统的参与者的终生结果与预期结果不一致，则该系统是非遍历的。

# ↩

Then , in the second half of the book, I described three strategies to manage non-ergodicity:

然后，在本书的后半部分，我描述了三种应对非遍历性的策略：

– The barbell strategy: avoid exposing all of yourself to a risk of ruin, no matter how small.

– 杠铃策略：避免让自己陷入毁灭的风险，无论风险多么小。

– Skin in the game: ensure that the dangerous gets removed, fast.

– 利益攸关：确保危险因素迅速消除。

– Redistribution is good for you, even if you’re above average.

即使你的收入高于平均水平，重新分配收入对你也是有好处的。

The last few pages of this book contain quotable bits and information about me and my other books. Enjoy !

本书最后几页收录了一些精彩语录以及关于我和我的其他作品的信息。敬请欣赏！
