Winning Long-Term Games

赢得长期比赛

The key to winning long-term games is to stop playing them as a succession of separate short-term games.

赢得长期比赛的关键在于停止将比赛视为一系列独立的短期比赛。

Yet , most people take the opposite approach. Here are three examples:

然而，大多数人却采取相反的做法。以下是三个例子：

  • The manager who sees each interaction with her team as a separate game. Every time she talks to her subordinates, it’s to get things done rather than develop their skills. As a result, she fails to build the long-term assets (a competent team) she needs in order to win her long-term game (a successful career).
    这位管理者将与团队的每一次互动都视为一场独立的游戏。她每次与下属交谈，都是为了完成任务，而不是为了培养他们的技能。结果，她无法建立起赢得长期目标（成功职业生涯）所需的长期资产（一支称职的团队）。
  • The spouse who lies to avoid responsibility. If lying has, say, a 1% chance of being discovered, it is a great short-term tactic (it succeeds 99% of the time) but a terrible long-term strategy (if you lie once a week, you have a 99.5% chance of getting caught over a decade).
    配偶为了逃避责任而撒谎。如果撒谎被发现的概率只有 1%，那么这是一种很好的短期策略（成功率高达 99%），但从长远来看却是一种糟糕的策略（如果你每周撒谎一次，那么十年后你被发现的概率高达 99.5%）。
  • The solopreneur who sends weekly emails to their mailing list and sees each as a separate game. They consume their audience’s trust to generate more sales within a single email instead of building trust to create more sales within a few months.
    有些个体创业者每周都会向邮件列表发送邮件，并将每次发送都视为一场独立的游戏。他们为了在单封邮件中提升销量而消耗受众的信任，而不是通过几个月的时间来建立信任，最终实现销售增长。

These three examples show that approaching long-term games as a succession of separate short-term games is a bad strategy despite working great over short time horizons.

这三个例子表明，尽管在短期内效果很好，但将长期博弈视为一系列独立的短期博弈是一种糟糕的策略。

In “ Winning Long - Term Games ,” Luca guides the reader into designing strategies that not only have a long-term horizon but also leverage the long term to gain an edge against anyone with shorter time horizons and make success all but inevitable.

在《赢得长期博弈》一书中，卢卡指导读者设计策略，这些策略不仅具有长远的眼光，而且还利用长远优势来对抗那些眼光较短的人，从而使成功几乎成为必然。

Winning Long - Term Games is planned to be published in the first half of 2024.

《赢得长期游戏》计划于 2024 年上半年出版。

Best Practices for Operational Excellence (3 rd ed.)

卓越运营最佳实践（第3版）

FURTHER READINGS

延伸阅读

“ Ergodicity Economics ,” by Ole Peters and Alex Adamou . The technical text of reference, in my opinion. I also recommend reading the other papers by the same authors.

《遍历性经济学》（Ole Peters 和 Alex Adamou 合著）在我看来是权威的技术参考书。我还建议阅读这两位作者的其他论文。

“ Skin in The Game ” and “ Antifragile ,” by Nassim Nicholas Taleb , on many of the topics discussed in this book.

纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布的《风险自负》和《反脆弱》探讨了本书中讨论的许多主题。

“ The Dynamics of Risk - Taking ,” by Luca Dellanna (myself), on how damage propagates, how it becomes irreversible, and dynamic considerations.

《冒险的动态》，作者 Luca Dellanna（本人），探讨了损害如何传播、如何变得不可逆转以及动态因素。

“ Ergodicity and Digital Culture ,” by Spear of Lugh , on how ergodicity influences the spread of cultures.

《遍历性和数字文化》，作者斯皮尔·卢格，探讨遍历性如何影响文化的传播。

“ The Precautionary Principle (with Application to the Genetic Modification of Organisms ),” by Nassim Nicholas Taleb , Rupert Read , Raphael Douady , Joseph Norman , and Yaneer Bar - Yam .

《预防原则（及其在生物体基因改造中的应用）》，作者：纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布、鲁珀特·里德、拉斐尔·杜阿迪、约瑟夫·诺曼和亚尼尔·巴尔-亚姆。

“ Risk , Intuition , and Common Sense ,” Harry Crane’s Substack .

“风险、直觉和常识”，哈里·克莱恩的 Substack。

除非另有说明，所有图片均来自 Pixabay、Unsplash 或 Wikimedia Commons。

QUOTABLE BITS

可引用部分

When people say that childhood was the best time of their lives, they usually miss reversibility.

人们常说童年是他们一生中最美好的时光，但他们往往忽略了时间的可逆性。

Avoiding the risks of ruin is how you get ahead in the long term.

避免破产的风险才是长期成功的关键。

Maximizing the expected returns of your choices is a good strategy if and only if mistakes and misfortunes are reversible.

只有当错误和不幸是可逆的，最大化选择的预期收益才是一个好的策略。

What is optimal in the presence of reversibility is stupid otherwise, and the other way around.

在可逆性条件下最优解在其他情况下就是愚蠢的，反之亦然。

It is not the best ones who succeed. It is the best ones of those who survive.

最终成功的并非最优秀的人，而是那些幸存下来的人中最优秀的人。

Performance is subordinate to survival.

生存才是最重要的。

Over the short term, consequences that apply beyond the short term do not matter. Over the long term, they do.

短期内，那些会影响到短期之后的后果无关紧要；但从长远来看，它们却至关重要。

Irreversibility absorbs future gains.

不可逆性会吞噬未来的收益。

Distinguish between calculated risks whose consequences you can recover from and recklessness whose consequences might permanently debilitate you. There is a sweet spot where you expose yourself to the former but not the latter – that’s a good place to aim.

区分可以承受后果的经过深思熟虑的风险和可能造成永久性残疾的鲁莽行为。存在一个最佳平衡点，既能让你承担前者的风险，又能避免后者的风险——这才是应该努力的方向。

Any form of “game-over” nullifies future gains, bringing the average down.

任何形式的“游戏结束”都会抵消未来的收益，从而拉低平均值。

For real people, the limitation on the number of times they can play can transform their lifetime outcome of a gamble into negative.

对于普通人来说，赌博次数的限制可能会使他们一生的赌博结果变成负面的。

It is pointless to envy someone with whom you wouldn’t trade places in all parallel universes.

嫉妒一个你即使在所有平行宇宙中也不会和他交换位置的人是毫无意义的。

A system can work well on average and still fail locally.

一个系统平均而言可能运行良好，但局部仍可能出现故障。

As an individual, you do not care whether the system works on average. You care if it works for you.

作为个人，你并不关心系统平均而言是否有效，你只关心它是否对你有效。

Central organizations are only efficient to the central observer.

中央组织只有对中央观察者而言才是高效的。

The best strategy depends on whether you are the gamble or the gambler.

最佳策略取决于你是赌徒还是被赌徒。

The survival of a population does not coincide with the survival of its members, not all of them.

一个种群的生存并不等同于其所有成员的生存。

Whether you live in an ergodic world determines what is rational and what isn’t.

你是否生活在一个遍历性世界中，决定了什么是理性的，什么是不理性的。

For most people, what matters is how much their lifetime outcome diverges from the population outcome in the medium term.

对大多数人来说，重要的是他们一生的结果与中期人口结果之间的差异有多大。

Moods are tools to adapt to environments with clustered resources.

情绪是适应资源分散环境的工具。

Moderately moody people tend to be more efficient than moodless ones.

情绪波动适中的人往往比情绪完全没有情绪的人效率更高。

Natural selection is inevitable, but we can avoid it at any given level by pushing it towards a lower one.

自然选择是不可避免的，但我们可以通过将其推向更低的层次来避免在任何给定层次上发生自然选择。

A population can decrease its exposure to irreversibility by exposing its members to it.

群体可以通过让其成员接触不可逆转的因素来降低自身遭受不可逆转风险的可能性。

In a non-ergodic world, you benefit from redistribution even if you’re giving more than you’re receiving.

在非遍历性世界中，即使你付出的多于所得，你也能从再分配中受益。

It pays to redistribute, so that for each step forward, you only make a partial step back.

重新分配资源是值得的，这样每向前迈一步，你只会后退一部分。

Ergodicity is a property of an activity, its participants, and the exposure of the latter to the former.

遍历性是活动、参与者以及参与者与活动接触的共同属性。

Behavioral change is non-ergodic. The distribution of efforts matters.

行为改变并非遍历过程。努力的分配至关重要。

Sustainability is often a larger obstacle to performance than talent.

可持续性往往比天赋更能阻碍绩效的提升。

The easiest way to increase performance is to narrow the time frame over which it is measured. Sadly , it is also the easiest way to produce unsustainable performance.

提高绩效最简单的方法是缩短衡量绩效的时间范围。遗憾的是，这也是导致绩效无法持续的最简单方法。

The easiest way to hide problems is to increase the scope of measurement.

掩盖问题的最简单方法就是扩大测量范围。

Problems grow the size they need for them to be acknowledged.

问题只有发展到一定程度才会被人重视。
